title: Ultra-hypofractionated radiotherapy with focal boost for high-risk localized prostate cancer (HYPO-RT-PC-boost): in silico evaluation with histological reference
creator: Erik Nilsson, Anneli Nilsson, Joakim Jonsson, Kristina Sandgren, Josefine Grefve, Jan Axelsson, Angsana K Lindberg, Karin Söderkvist, Camilla T Karlsson, Björn Zackrisson, Sara Strandberg, Katrine Riklund, Anders Bergh, Mathieu Moreau, Adalsteinn Gunnlaugsson, Lars E Olsson, Tufve Nyholm
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and purposeThe study aims to evaluate dosimetric properties of hypofractionated treatment plans integrating focal boost, using registered whole-mount histopathology (WMHP) as reference standard.MethodsFifteen men from the PAMP trial (EudraCT: 2015-005046-55) were included. Participants had ≥ 1 ISUP Grade group ≥ 4 lesion and underwent [68Ga]prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (PET/mpMRI) and [11C]Acetate-PET/computed tomography before radical prostatectomy. Four radiation oncologists delineated gross tumor volumes (GTVs) on PSMA-PET/mpMRI. Sixty treatment plans were optimized, one per GTV and patient.

title: Longitudinal single-cell and TCR repertoire profiling characterizes clonal entrapment in patients with pMMR/MSS locally advanced rectal cancer
creator: Zhichun Tang, Mingxuan Zhu, Shidong Zhao, Dazhi Pang, Yancheng Cui, Guole Lin, Aiwen Wu, Yilin Lin, Xinyang Jiang, Wei Zhang, Nan Xiong, Changjiang Yang, Caihong Wang, Shan Wang, Yingjiang Ye, Fan Bai, Zhanlong Shen
description: Elevated intratumoral immune inflammation prior to treatment is typically associated with better outcomes in hot tumors treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). However, we observed a paradox in pMMR/MSS locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) patients, where a subset with elevated baseline immune inflammation exhibited worse outcomes after combined radiotherapy and ICI treatment compared with patients with minimal immune inflammation.

title: Family history-adjusted age recommendation for initiating breast cancer screening: 7-year follow-up from a prospective cohort study
creator: Juan Zhu, Le Wang, Weiwei Gong, Xue Li, Youqing Wang, Chen Zhu, Huizhang Li, Lei Shi, Chen Yang, Lingbin Du
description: rly detection,[2] Family history—a major nonmodifiable risk factor—significantly influences individual breast cancer risk and age of onset, warranting tailored screening strategies. In China, national initiatives such as the Cancer Screening Program in Urban China and the Breast and Cervical Cancer Project for Rural Women have improved early detection.

title: Sequential Single-Conduit Antegrade Flow Reconstruction for Multivessel Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia After Failed Endovascular Therapy
creator: Gökçen Özkan, Cihan Yücel, Helin El Kılıç, Abdullah Burak Balcı, Necdet Kılıçaslan, Zakir İbrahim Kılınç, Hakan Yırgın, Yasir Musa Kesgin
description: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) with multivessel occlusive disease remains challenging when endovascular therapy fails. We describe sequential antegrade reconstruction of the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) and celiac artery using a single 8-mm Dacron conduit originating from the supraceliac aorta. A 59-year-old man with severe malnutrition presented with progressive postprandial abdominal pain and substantial weight loss.

title: Correction
creator: Ramos Junior, O. J. F., Veiga, N. S., Berretta, A. A., & Alvares, T. S.
description:
has now been included and republished in the original article. The below mentioned is the Figure 3 which is now included in the original article.

Representative ultrasound images and echo intensity measurements. Images were taken before and 2 hours after EIMD for the PLA group (A) and the EPP-AF group (B). RF = rectus femoris muscle; VI = vastus intermedius muscle.

title: Involving people with lived experiences in the study of a behavioral stress-recovery e-intervention for myocardial infarction patients younger than 55 with cardiac distress: a study protocol
creator: Niclas Almén, Ulf O. E. Elofsson, Claudia T. Lissåker, Claes Held, Henrik Nygård, Erik M. G. Olsson
description: BackgroundPublic and patient involvement and engagement (PPIE) is increasingly valued for improving the quality and relevance of health research. Patient research partners (PRPs) offer lived experience of a previous myocardial infarction and cardiac distress that can enhance study design and implementation.

title: ARHGAP18 complexes with both YAP and Merlin and is required for basal actin bundles
creator: Emma C Murray, Gillian M Hodge, Khanh Pham, Shane Fraher, Leighton S Lee, Cameron AR Mitchell, Namya Manoj, Christine E Schaner Tooley, Yongho Bae, Andrew T Lombardo, Alpha Yap
description: The organization of the cell's cytoskeletal filaments is coordinated through a complex network of signaling cascades activated by both internal and external cues. Two major actin regulatory pathways are signal transduction through Rho family GTPases and growth and proliferation signaling through the Hippo pathway.

title: Brazilian Registry of Sjögren’s Disease (BRAS): a full picture of Sjögren’s disease in Brazil
creator: Valéria Valim, Samira Tatiyama Miyamoto, Fabiola Reis de Oliveira, Érica Vieira Serrano, Laura Caldas dos Santos, Roberta de Almeida Pernambuco, Simone Appenzeller, Juliana Markus, Leandro Augusto Tanure, Maria Lúcia Lemos Lopes, Rafael Coradin, Aysa César Pinheiro, Vanessa Hax, Aiessa Zanchett Fedr
description: Cohort studies are essential for elucidating disease progression, guiding research priorities, and identifying gaps in diagnosis and treatment. This manuscript presents the protocol and preliminary findings of the Brazilian Registry on Sjögren’s Disease (BRAS), a national, prospective cohort supported by the Brazilian Society of Rheumatology (SBR).

title: Human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived cardiomyocytes improve recovery from myocardial infarction in non-human primates
creator: Xumin Guan, Pengfei Zhang, Qian Wang, Yuehui Zhang, Yunfan Zhang, He Zhang, Hang Zhang, Wanxiang Jiang, Yanxia Wu, Xijie Wang, Dongjin Wang, Jiaxian Wang, Ling Gao
description: BackgroundThe transplantation of human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) represents a promising next-generation cell therapy for repairing injured myocardium. However, the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of these cells in non-human primates (NHPs) with myocardial infarction (MI) have not been systematically investigated.

title: Cohort Profile: Shanghai University of Sport (SUS) Longitudinal Cohort Study of Alumni Health Tracking
creator: Huanyu Wang, Ruwen Wang, Qin Sun, Shanshan Guo, Kaiqing Lin, Qianqian Tian, Keneilwe Kenny Kaudimba, Mingjia Yang, Tiemin Liu, Ru Wang
description: BackgroundThe Shanghai University of Sport (SUS) Longitudinal Cohort Study (SUS Cohort) was established to investigate the influence of lifestyle and modifiable behavioral factors in early adulthood on the development of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) later in life. The cohort aims to identify novel biomarkers and explore mechanisms underlying chronic diseases using a multi-omics approach.

title: Critical appraisal of progress and challenges in tuberculosis preventive treatment in the Western Pacific Region: a situational analysis of seven high tuberculosis burden countries
creator: Muhamad Khizar, Ehsanullah Alokozay, Muhammad Junaid, Najibullah Alokozay
description: We commend Oh et al.’s recent analysis of TB preventive treatment (TPT) in the Western Pacific Region, but note important gaps and ways forward. We first caution that reliance on routine program data may overestimate gains. For example, China’s passive surveillance misses ≈20% of cases [1]. Prospective cohorts or integrated surveillance including clinical databases could validate coverage estimates.

title: Impact of coronavirus disease on the incidence rate of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus among hospitalized patients with lung cancer: a nationwide retrospective cohort study in Japan
creator: Yasutaka Ihara, Hisafumi Kihara, Waki Imoto, Naoto Okada, Hiroshi Kakeya, Yukihiro Kaneko
description: BackgroundPatients with lung cancer are at increased risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infection, which prolongs treatment and worsens prognosis. Therefore, preventing MRSA infection is critically important in this population. We aimed to investigate whether the incidence rate of MRSA among patients with lung cancer declined after the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic, owing to the widespread reinforcement of hand-rub use.

title: Recurrent giant cell tumor of the right distal tibia: A case report
creator: Nisha D. Barole, Kuntal P. Godde, Vaishnavi D. Rajurkar, Shubhangi P. Raut
description: Giant cell tumors (GCTs) of the bone are neoplasms that are characterized by benign, locally aggressive behavior and occur most commonly in the young population. It is usually located at epiphyseal areas of bones, especially distal femur and proximal tibia.

title: Multi spectroscopic investigations with molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation of the binding mechanism of molnupiravir to bovine serum albumin
creator: Fotouh R. Mansour, Nada Elhosary, Samar H. Elagamy, Aya Barseem, Amira H. Kamal
description: Molnupiravir (MOL) is a recently developed oral antiviral drug. MOL has been clinically evaluated for its efficacy against COVID-19. In this work, we utilize UV-absorption spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, synchronous fluorescence, molecular docking and molecular dynamic (MD) simulation to study the interaction between MOL and bovine serum albumin (BSA).

title: Comparison of fluoroscopy time and procedure time of endovascular interventions with and without prior angiography simulator training: a meta-analysis
creator: Timo C Meine, Johannes M Dorl, Anselm A Derda, Nima Mahmoudi, Hans-Jonas Meyer
description: BackgroundAngiography simulator training (AST) can help to train important clinical aspects of complex angiography procedures before real patient contact. The aim of the present analysis was to synthesize the results of studies on endovascular interventions performed by interventionalists with and without AST in a meta-analysis.MethodsA systematic literature research was performed in PubMed, Web-of-Science and CINAHL to identify all relevant studies.

title: Differential LTR-retrotransposon dynamics across polyploidization, speciation, domestication, and improvement of cotton (Gossypium)
creator: Lucía Campos-Dominguez, Raúl Castanera, Corrinne E Grover, Jonathan F Wendel, Josep M Casacuberta
description: BackgroundTransposable elements are major components of plant genomes and major drivers of plant genome evolution. The cotton genus (Gossypium) is an excellent evolutionary model for polyploidization, speciation, domestication, and crop improvement. Here, we implement genome and pangenome analyses to study in detail the dynamics of LTR-retrotransposons during the cotton evolution.

title: Public readiness for anaphylaxis emergencies in Al-Baha Region, Saudi Arabia: A cross-sectional study
creator: Mohammad I. Barnawi, Muaid H. Morad, Nujud A. Alzahrani, Nada H. Alqarni, Daniyah A. Alghamdi, Hanin A. Alamri, Wajd S. Alghamdi
description: Context:Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening systemic allergic reaction requiring prompt recognition and epinephrine administration. Public preparedness for anaphylaxis has not been previously assessed in Al-Baha region of Saudi Arabia.Aim:To measure the level of public knowledge, awareness, and practice readiness regarding anaphylaxis among adult residents of Al-Baha region.Setting and Design:A cross-sectional, descriptive-analytical survey conducted in Al-Baha region between February and April 2026.

title: Targeting PP2A in cancer: an underrated option
creator: Fabio Sarais, Finja Krempien, Caroline Koehn, Lara Brewing, Carl Friedrich Classen, Michael Walter, Olia Shokraie
description: Protein phosphatase 2A plays a central role in modulating multiple signaling pathways, including PI3K, EGFR, Myc, WNT, JAK/STAT, RAS/MAPK, and NF-κB, which are frequently dysregulated in cancer. Although PP2A is broadly considered a tumor suppressor due to its frequent functional loss in tumors, its biological role is highly context-dependent and varies across cancer types and stages.

title: Cholestasis as a complication in Kawasaki disease: an atypical clinical presentation
creator: Jiaxiang Hong, Chenchen Liu, Xunmin Wang, Xing Rong, Rongzhou Wu, Maoping Chu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeCholestasis is an uncommon complication in Kawasaki disease (KD) that impacts the digestive system. This study aimed to examine the clinical characteristics and associated risk factors of KD complicated by cholestasis.MethodsAmong the 3026 KD patients admitted to Yuying Children’s Hospital, affiliated with Wenzhou Medical University, from January 1, 2008, to December 31, 2020, all 72 children with cholestasis were included in the study.

title: Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery versus laparoscopy for salpingo-oophorectomy and adnexectomy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Suhaib Khayat, Mohammad Khojah
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) and laparoscopic surgeries have widely been utilized in gynecologic surgeries including adnexectomy and hysterectomy. The aim of conducting this comprehensive meta-analysis is to evaluate the peri- and post-operative safety and clinical efficacy of vNOTES versus laparoscopic surgeries for the indications of unilateral or bilateral salpingectomy, unilateral or bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, oophorectomy, and adnexectomy with or without hysterectomies for gynecological pathologies.

title: Effectiveness and safety of tacrolimus in systemic lupus erythematosus with various clinical manifestations: a retrospective real-world study
creator: Wei Bai, Hui Luo, Huaxiang Wu, Xinwang Duan, Jian Xu, Cheng Zhao, Qinghua Zou, Xiaofei Shi, Yuehong Huo, Zhen Chen, Jiuliang Zhao, Xinping Tian, Qian Wang, Xiaomei Leng, Yanhong Wang, Yan Zhao, Mengtao Li, Xiaofeng Zeng
description: ObjectiveThis study evaluated the real-world effectiveness and safety of tacrolimus as a steroid-sparing maintenance therapy alone without additional biologics or immunosuppressive medications in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), particularly in mild, non–new-onset cases, with a focus on glucocorticoid-sparing effects and multi-organ remission.

title: A cross-sectional study of patients’ morbidity profiles and doctors’ drug prescribing patterns from outpatient departments of a community health centre from a district of Uttarakhand
creator: Puneet Ohri, Megha Luthra, Mohd. Anshar, Sachin Kumar
description: Introduction:A study of the pattern of disease occurrence provides inputs for diagnosis and treatment, and is a tool for administrators and policy makers. Periodic prescription analysis increases treatment effectiveness, provides feedback and decreases adverse effects.Materials and Methods:All patients attending the outpatient departments (OPDs) of the selected community health centre during the study period were included.

title: Effects of a 12-week Tai Chi Chuan combined with walking program on physical and mental parameters of older adults: rationale and methodological protocol for a randomized controlled trial
creator: Breno Berny Vasconcelos, Matheus Pintanel Freitas, Inácio Crochemore-Silva, Cristine Lima Alberton
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundTai Chi Chuan is a Chinese martial art style that integrates slow and rhythmic movements with synchronized breathing, classified as a mind–body modality. Its practice has been shown to positively impact health markers in various populations, including older individuals.

title: A Targeted Liposomal Delivery System for Hydrophobic Antitumor Compounds Using the Example of a 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydroisoquinoline Derivative
creator: G. M. Proshkina, O. N. Ashirov, M. N. Zharkov, A. Al-Khadj Aioub, V. I. Vinogradova, D. Zhu, R. Yan, Sh. S. Azimova, E. I. Shramova, N. A. Pyataev, S. M. Deyev
description: Cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide, after cardiovascular disorders. One of the main constraints of anticancer agents is their limited water solubility, which complicates preclinical in vivo studies. In this work, we propose a versatile approach for stabilizing hydrophobic antitumor agents using liposomes based on natural phospholipids.

title: Reconstruction of a Self-sustaining System of Oscillating Glycolytic Reactions in Artificial Microreactors
creator: O. M. Alekhina, P. V. Bashkirov, A. S. Silantyev, S. P. Dudik, D. S. Matyushkina, O. V. Shcherbakova, V. M. Govorun
description: Synthetic cell design is one of the daunting challenges of modern biology. While the genome synthesis problem has already been solved technologically, the understanding of the molecular composition of the intracellular environment required for initiating artificial life still remains elusive. One of the mechanisms of self-organization in prebiotic systems is the oscillatory processes (oscillations) arising from feedback regulation.

title: CarpeDeam: a de novo metagenome assembler for heavily damaged ancient datasets
creator: Louis Kraft, Johannes Söding, Martin Steinegger, Annika Jochheim, Peter Wad Sackett, Antonio Fernandez-Guerra, Gabriel Renaud
description: De novo assembly of ancient metagenomic datasets is a challenging task. Ultra-short fragment size and characteristic postmortem damage patterns of sequenced ancient DNA molecules leave current tools ill-equipped for ideal assembly. We present CarpeDeam, a novel damage-aware de novo assembler designed specifically for ancient metagenomic samples.

title: Beyond distance: integrating economic burden into large-scale primary healthcare accessibility analysis
creator: Bin Zhu, Liutong Chen, Yifei He, Ning Zhang, Hao Xue, Samir Bhatt, Minghui Ren, Ying Mao
description: BackgroundAccess to primary healthcare (PHC) services is a critical determinant of population health outcomes and a key indicator of health system performance. However, comprehensive methods for batch assessment of PHC accessibility and the associated economic burden are relatively scarce. This gap is particularly evident in developing countries, where accessibility challenges are often more pronounced.

title: Updating deficits in subjective cognitive decline: A differential pattern of executive dysfunction across clinical stages
creator: Yuetan Wang, Wenni Zhan, Zhuoyan Wu, Yan Zhang, Zhuo Ma, Xiaobin Ding
description: Identifying objective cognitive markers in the preclinical stage of Alzheimer's disease (AD), particularly in Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD), is critical for early intervention. While executive function comprises three core components (inhibition, updating/switching), their impairment trajectory during the SCD-to-Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) progression remains unclear.

title: Self-reported mental distress in the United States: a Bayesian analysis of the spatial structure over the COVID-19 pandemic across age groups
creator: Carles Comas, Albert Martínez, Angel Blanch
description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 had an outstanding impact on well-being and mental health, which might have elicited geographical variations over time. This study examines the eventual impact of COVID-19 on self-reported mental distress in the mainland USA.AimsThere were two main aims. First, to evaluate the pre-pandemic (2019; ) and post-pandemic (2021; ) mental distress spatial distribution.

title: Direct medical cost analysis of breast cancer treatment at Jimma University Medical Center: a provider perspective
creator: Gebeyehu Jeldu Edessa, Kidist Adamu Kare, Aleka Jeldu Edessa, Dawit Wolde Daka
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionBreast cancer is an evolving non-communicable disease and a global disease burden, which accounts for a momentous portion of worldwide mortality and morbidity with significant economic impacts. In low- and middle-income countries like Ethiopia, the most common problem with cancer treatment is scarcity of medical resources, and financial supply, for providing care, which includes expensive medical costs, cost of service provision, and medical equipment.

title: Effect of Anti-thyroid Peroxidase Antibodies on Assisted Reproductive Technologies Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Nora Nerdrum Stølan, Pernille Fog Svendsen, Anna Klajnbard, Nina Freiesleben Mørch
description: Background:Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies (TPOAbs) are common among women of reproductive age, especially in assisted reproductive technologies (ART). Their impact on early embryological outcomes remains unclear. Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) has been proposed to overcome possible adverse effects of TPOAbs in the follicular fluid.

title: Effects of kinesio tape on countermovement jump kinetic variables in physically active females with flat feet before and after fatigue: a randomized controlled trial
creator: Zeynab Nickpey, Sahar Boozari, Abbas Farjad Pezeshk
description: BackgroundFlatfoot, characterized by a reduced medial longitudinal arch, alters lower-limb biomechanics and affects vertical ground reaction force (vGRF) during dynamic tasks like jumping. Kinesio taping (KT) is often used to support foot posture; however, its efficacy under high-load conditions—such as jumping, which increases arch stress, and fatigue, which reduces muscular support—remains unclear.

title: Replication and replicability as epistemic opportunity for the humanities: reflections on a Rembrandt attribution case study
creator: Charlotte C. S. Rulkens, Rik Peels, Maartje Stols-Witlox, Lex Bouter
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Motivated by the ‘replication crisis’ that deeply impacted the biomedical, natural, and social sciences, we conducted a case study to examine the strengths and limitations of replication in the humanities. Specifically, we replicated an art historical Rembrandt attribution study.

title: Sophora alopecuroides biflavones glycoside, isolated from Sophora alopecuroides, inhibits the secretion of hepatitis B virus surface antigen through direct interaction with its antigenic loop domain
creator: Ya Wang, Linlin Wang, Ge Yang, Lijun Qiao, Rongmei Gao, Huiqiang Wang, Haiyan Yan, Kun Wang, Shuo Wu, Hua Huang, Yuhuan Li
description: BackgroundHigh levels of circulating hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) contribute to the dysfunction of the host immune response against HBV and the persistence of viral infection. This study aimed to investigate the effects and mechanisms of Sophora alopecuroides biflavones glycoside (SABG), isolated from the traditional herbal medicine Sophora alopecuroides, on HBV replication and HBsAg secretion.

title: Association between SHR and mortality in critically ill patients with CVD: a retrospective analysis and machine learning approach
creator: Wanlu Zhou, Junxi Liao, Ting Wu, Jingjia Yu
description: BackgroundThe stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), a measure of glucose metabolism, has emerged as a novel indicator of illness severity in critically ill patients. This study aims to evaluate the association between SHR and adverse outcomes in critically ill patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD).MethodsClinical data of 1,913 critically ill patients with CVD were extracted from the MIMIC-IV database.

title: Site-Specific Trends in Tumor Distribution, Treatment Patterns, and Survival in Head and Neck Cancer: A SEER Database Analysis *
creator: Christopher Stewart, JB Eyring, Abbigail Niewchas, Joseph Hanny, Grant Sanders, Alex Otto, Randall Hansen, Kent McIntire
description: IntroductionHead and neck cancer (HNC) management has evolved significantly with the introduction of organ-preservation protocols and changing disease etiology.ObjectiveTo analyze site-specific trends in tumor distribution, staging, treatment modality, and survival outcomes using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) program.MethodsA retrospective analysis of 288,132 malignant HNC cases from the SEER program (2000–2021) was performed.

title: Improving the Polyphenol Profile, Antioxidant and Antiglycation Activity of Onion Outer Scales with Chamomile Treatment
creator: Valerija Vujčić Bok, Sanja Gagić, Lucija Rubinić, Ivana Šola, Petra Kašnjar Perković, Nika Celinić, Sandra Jurić, Željan Maleš
description: SUMMARYResearch backgroundThe outer scales of common onion (Allium cepa L.) are often discarded as biological waste but they can be an interesting source of polyphenols with antioxidant and antidiabetic properties that can be used in the food and pharmaceutical industries.Experimental approachThe aim of this study is to use dried chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla L.

title: Process evaluation of the residential care transition module
creator: Dana P Urbanski, Robyn W Birkeland, Elle A Albers, David L Roth, Zachary G Baker, Allison M Gustavson, Hawking Yam, Joseph E Gaugler
description: BackgroundDementia caregiver intervention research often lacks focus on mechanisms of benefit. This study addresses this gap through a process evaluation of the Residential Care Transition Module (RCTM), a telehealth intervention designed to assist family caregivers of persons with dementia post-institutionalization, consisting of six sessions with flexible ad hoc support over a 12-month period.

title: Community-Based Accompaniment for Adolescents and Young Adults Transitioning into Adult HIV Care: Protocol of a Randomized Control Trial Evaluating the “PASEO” Intervention in Urban Peru
creator: Molly F Franke, Renato Errea, Alyson Nunez, Milagros Wong, Hugo Sánchez, Carmen C Contreras, Jerome T Galea, Erika Gonzales, Isabel Ccota, Cristina Chávez, Alicia Ramos, Karen Finnegan, Diana Mejía, Jimena Ruiz-Cardenas, Grecia Herrera, Nicole Ocasio-Martinez, Letizia Trevisi, Martha Vibbert, Sonya
description: We describe a randomized controlled trial evaluating a nine-month community-based accompaniment intervention (PASEO) to improve HIV outcomes and well-being among adolescents and young adults living with HIV (AYALWH) entering adult-centered HIV care in Lima, Peru. Participants (ages 14–23) are individually randomized (1:1) to PASEO or a modestly enhanced standard of care, with randomization stratified by health facility and caregiver support.

title: Unraveling the nexus between domestic violence and women’s self-rated health status in sub-Saharan Africa: a multi-country investigation for advancing SDG 3 and 5
creator: Alex Bawuah, Michael Sarfo, Jacob Oppong Nkansah, Edward Kwabena Ameyaw
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundDomestic violence against women (DVAW) is recognised globally as a violation of human rights and a public health concern. This study explores the relationship between DVAW and women’s self-rated health status (SRHS).

title: Associations between reproductive factors and frailty in middle-aged and older women: evidence from the China health and retirement longitudinal study
creator: Xiaobing Xian, Jie Xiang, Shiwei Cao, Wanting Tang, Yao Wu, Jiaxia Li, Shiqin Ren, Yuanyuan Wang, Kun Shen
description: BackgroundAmid global aging, frailty significantly threatens the health of middle-aged and older women. This study is the first to explore the association between reproductive factors (age at first livebirth, number of biological children, reproductive period, age at menopause, age at menarche, and history of abortion) and frailty among middle-aged and elderly Chinese women.

title: From Collection to Collaboration: Building Ethical Frameworks for Genetic Research
creator: Devin A. Madden, Emerson Dusic, Isabella E. Rios, Kimberly Zayhowski, L Jude Tantay, Nasa Sinnott-Armstrong, Rodrigo Aguayo-Romero, Sima Rabinowitz, Michelle A. Ramos, Kellan Baker, Sari L. Reisner, Carol R. Horowitz
description: Transgender, nonbinary, and gender diverse (TNGD) communities are not routinely included as partners in the research that will impact them. The expansion of genomic and gender identity data collection has allowed researchers to explore transgender identity genomics research (TIGR), or associations between genomics and gender identity.

title: Stronger Together: a community-based intervention using Behaviour Change Wheel to promote healthier lifestyles among women with low socioeconomic status: a feasibility study
creator: Samah Alageel, Reem Alsukait, Amal Alharbi, Lisa Bilal, Haifa Aldakhil, Yasmin Altwaijri
description: BackgroundSocioeconomic status (SES) significantly influences individuals’ health behaviours and outcomes. Women with lower income levels show a higher prevalence of non-communicable diseases. Community-based interventions can improve health behaviours, but such programmes are scarce in Saudi Arabia. This highlights the need for research on the feasibility and preliminary outcomes of these approaches for women with low SES.

title: Reengaging Rural Research Participants After Two Decades: The NC Life Study’s Recruitment Challenges in an Era of Funding Uncertainty
creator: Emily Forrest Hutchens, Marina Pearsall, Robert Faris, Alberto Valido Delgado, Liann Tucker, Nisha Gottfredson O’Shea, Tamara Taggart
description: The North Carolina Life (NC Life, R01DA056264, MPI: O’Shea and Taggart) study is a 20-year follow-up to a groundbreaking adolescent study (R01DA013459, PI: Ennett), which examined the health behaviors of over 8,000 racially diverse adolescents in rural North Carolina communities during the early 2000s.

title: Intra‐operative oxygen concentration could affect postoperative morbidity—results of a randomised controlled feasibility trial (PULSE Ox)
creator: A F Cumpstey, J Stygall, A D Clark, M Minnion, H Moyses, D S Martin, M R Edwards, M Feelisch, M PW Grocott
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryThe World Health Organisation recommends that all anaesthetised patients receive FIO2 0.8 during surgery to reduce the risk of surgical site infections but did not consider the effect this might have on other clinical outcomes. A Cochrane systematic review concluded that insufficient evidence exists for routinely administering high oxygen concentrations intra‐operatively to reduce surgical site infections, and that doing so might increase mortality. A feasibility trial was conducted looking at the feasibility of controlling intra‐operative FIO2 and measuring systemic redox state.

title: Dual PDE4/10A inhibition restores CREB1 function and enhances neuronal resilience in models of alzheimer's disease
creator: Xiaoli Rong, Xia Yao, Haohui Fang, Johns Saji, Yu Qian, Jia-Xuan Gu, Meng-Yuan Yang, Peng Wei, Cai-Rui Liu, Bin Chen, Pian-Pian Zhao, Ching-Lung Cheung, Lin Bo, Hou-Feng Zheng
description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) involves cognitive decline, amyloid-beta (Aβ) accumulation, tau hyperphosphorylation, and neuroinflammation. CREB1, a key transcription factor for memory, is downregulated in AD, contributing to disease progression. Phosphodiesterases 4 and 10 (PDE4 and PDE10) are key enzymes that degrade cAMP, a second messenger involved in CREB signaling, synaptic plasticity, and neuroprotection.

title: Surgical Treatment of Rare Multiple Cardiac Myxomas: A 13-Year Clinical Experience at a Single Institution
creator: Wenjie Diao, Shengqiang Zhang, Shaofeng Yang, Yu Shi, Chongwen Shen, Chão Cai, Shicheng Xie, Chao Shi, Ge Liu
description: IntroductionCardiac myxoma (CM) is the most common primary cardiac tumor. Multiple CMs are rare and can lead to heart failure and arterial embolism. This study aimed to explore clinical characteristics, surgical treatment experience, and follow-up strategies for multiple CMs.MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on eight patients with multiple CMs who underwent surgical treatment.

title: Stakeholder perspectives on implementing person-centered transitional care in congenital heart disease: the STEPSTONES-Implement project
creator: Markus Saarijärvi, Milena Boczar, Sandra Skogby, Carina Sparud-Lundin, Ewa-Lena Bratt
description: BackgroundAdolescents with congenital heart disease (CHD) face substantial challenges during the transition from pediatric to adult care. The STEPSTONES transition program is a person-centered, evidence-based intervention designed to support this transition, and has shown efficacy in improving patient empowerment and disease-related knowledge. However, implementing complex health interventions like the STEPSTONES transition program in real-world settings remains difficult.

title: Towards a forward-looking ethnobiology: envisioning and co-creating biocultural futures
creator: Álvaro Fernández-Llamazares, Irene Teixidor-Toneu
description: In the face of accelerating environmental and socio-political changes, there is value in expanding the temporal scope of ethnobiology to more actively engage with the future. This perspective explores the potential of a forward-looking ethnobiology that incorporates methods from Futures Studies to co-envision and co-produce sustainable biocultural futures in partnership with Indigenous Peoples and local communities.

title: Relationship between intraoperative hypertension and postoperative ischemic stroke in neurosurgery—a retrospective cohort study
creator: Yu-Mei Feng, Qian-Yun Pang, Ya-Jun Yang, Hong-Liang Liu
description: BackgroundPostoperative ischemic stroke is a severe complication in neurosurgery, while intraoperative hypertension is a frequent event. However, their clinical relationship remains poorly understood.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study analyzed data from patients with brain tumors undergoing craniotomies between January 2017 and December 2023 at Chongqing University Cancer Hospital. Multivariate logistic regression identified risk factors for postoperative stroke.

title: The central neurometabolic fingerprint of persistent spinal pain syndrome type 2: A prospective [18F]FDG PET/CT neuroimaging study
creator: Lara S Burmeister, Max van Grinsven, Bert-Kristian van Roosendaal, Richard L Witkam, Inge Arnts, Stephanie Janssen, Jessica Wegener, Kris CP Vissers, Anne IJ Arens, Martin Gotthardt, Michael Rullmann, Dylan Henssen
description: Persistent spinal pain syndrome type 2 (PSPS-T2) is a disabling pain condition that persists after spinal surgery. While spinal cord stimulation (SCS) offers symptomatic relief, objective biomarkers to guide diagnosis and treatment are lacking.In this prospective cohort study, fifteen PSPS-T2 patients underwent dedicated [18F]FDG PET/CT brain imaging prior to SCS implantation.

title: Iron overload-induced ferroptosis in CD8+ T cells leads to functional abnormalities that promote endometriosis progression
creator: Shuang Wang, Le Xu, Xue Jiao, Xiaoyu Dong, Zhaoyang Zhong, Qianhui Ren, Xiaoxuan Liu, Ming Yuan, Guoyun Wang
description: BackgroundEndometriosis (EM) exhibits localised iron overload. However, the contribution of ferroptosis to EM pathogenesis remains unclear. We investigated how iron overload affects CD8⁺ T cell immune function and the underlying ferroptotic mechanisms.MethodsWe collected eutopic and ectopic endometrial tissues from 57 patients with stage III–IV EM and eutopic tissues from 31 controls.

title: GAS5 as a therapeutic target in breast cancer through apoptosis induction
creator: Alisha Badal, Zelinda Engelbrecht, Marianne J. Cronjé
description: The ongoing discovery of long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) involvement in carcinogenesis prevention and development has made significant strides in breast cancer therapeutics. lncRNA growth arrest-specific 5 (GAS5) is downregulated in breast cancer, and its downregulation is linked to advanced clinical staging and grading as well as poor survival outcomes.

title: Exploring structural connectivity alterations in CRPS: Insights from diffusion imaging and clinical correlates
creator: Martin Domin, Sebastian Strauss, Martin Lotze
description: In recent years, functional and structural brain imaging studies have accumulated heterogeneous evidence for brain-wide changes accompanying complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS). We tested possible white matter pathologies in patients with CRPS in the chronic stage in comparison to matched healthy controls.

title: STING activates ZBP1-mediated PANoptosis to defend against HSV-1 retinal infection
creator: Wei Liu, Haifeng Cui, Li Wang, Xiangyu Ge, Xingfei Zhu, Xingmiao Liang, Ziqing Chen, Yuwen Gan, Le Shi, Xuebin Hu, Xiaohu Ding, Zhengjie Xu, Xiaoling Liang, Lili Gong
description: Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) is the most common cause of infectious blindness and is a major cause of acute retinal necrosis (ARN), a severe condition marked by rapid necrosis of the retina. Effective treatments for HSV-1 retinal infection are limited to general antiviral drugs, which do not specifically target the underlying pathophysiology.

title: Reconsidering operability in late-presenting Taussig-Bing anomaly
creator: Bastien Provost, Francesco Bertelli, Rajiv Chaturvedi, Osami Honjo
description: n (PAH), which is considered a contraindication to definitive repair.1,2 However, medical therapy alone is not a long-standing solution.3 Management requires balancing the risks of chronic cyanosis against the perioperative hazards of surgery in the setting of elevated pulmonary vascular resistance while considering alternatives such as transplantation and palliation.4 Multimodal assessment and careful interpretation are critical to guide management.

title: Factors associated with burnout among Family and Community Medicine and Nursing residents: secondary analysis of a multicentre study
creator: Macarena Chacón-Docampo, Ángela Asensio-Martínez, Sara Rodríguez-Pastoriza, David Liñares-Mariñas, María Victoria Martín-Miguel, Cruz Bartolomé-Moreno, Clara González-Formoso, Ana Clavería
description: IntroductionHealthcare workers, especially medical and nursing residents, are exposed to situations that can lead to burnout. The main factors are organizational. However, it is more feasible for professionals to act on personal factors. There is a growing interest in interventions to prevent and reduce burnout.

title: Indications for the evaluation and supplementation of hypophosphatemia: an umbrella systematic review of reviews and guidelines
creator: Seraina Netzer, Lea Büchel, Annina E. Büchi, Carole E. Aubert
description: BackgroundHypophosphatemia, defined as low serum phosphate levels, is a frequent yet underrecognized condition associated with significant morbidity. Its etiology ranges from chronic conditions such as osteomalacia to acute states such as refeeding syndrome. This review systematically summarizes evidence and guidelines for phosphate testing and supplementation in adults, aiming to support clinical decision-making.MethodsWe conducted a systematic review following the PRISMA guidelines.

title: Perspectives on physical activity participation in middle-aged U.S. South Asian women at risk for type 2 diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study
creator: Nitha Mathew Joseph, Madelene Ottoson, Veronica J. Brady, Raji Pillai, Carina Katigbak, Sandy D. Jones, Larking L. Strong
description: ObjectiveIncreasing evidence supports the benefits of physical activity (PA) in lowering the risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among middle-aged women. Despite the increased risk for T2DM at a younger age, South Asian (SA) women in the United States (U.S.) have lower PA than men and have been studied to a lesser extent.

title: Chronically retained gauze (gossypiboma) resembling a mature cystic teratoma after Cesarean delivery: a case report
creator: Temesgen Tilahun
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundA foreign body left behind during an operation is a medico-legal issue. It is an infrequent but avoidable surgical complication, which must be kept in mind in any postoperative patient who presents with pain, infection, or palpable mass.Case summaryThe author presents a rare case of chronic gossypiboma following a Cesarean delivery in a 40-year-old woman, who was a Para III patient from Western Ethiopia. She had been experiencing dull, aching pain since her previous Cesarean section four years prior.

title: The “Eat Less Meat” one-month challenge: a randomized controlled trial of a meat reduction pledge intervention among French university students
creator: Lucile Marty, Manon Biehlmann, Anne Louveau, Delphine Poquet, Eric Robinson
description: BackgroundEncouraging the shift towards more plant-based diets in new generations is one of the major current challenges to preserve population and planetary health. Personal pledges to reduce meat consumption could motivate behaviour change, but have received limited scientific testing. We examined the effect of a “Eat Less Meat” one-month challenge on immediate and long-term meat consumption of university students.

title: Annelated N-heterocyclic carbene-derived organic redox system for consecutive visible-light photocatalysis
creator: Yu-Jia Liu, Xin Li, Ji-Xin Man, Can Chen, Man Li, Jia-Ling Zhu, Ying-Feng Han
description: Electron transfer is a fundamental process ubiquitous in both natural and artificial systems. The construction of organic redox systems serves as an ideal platform to explore this mechanism. The interconversion between different electronic structures endows them with unique photoelectric properties, enabling their promising applications in fields such as photocatalysis, organic batteries and electrochromic materials.

title: Drivers of managed entry agreements to reduce reimbursement challenges of orphan medicinal products: the development of a matrix
creator: Marcelien H E Callenbach, Sibren van den Berg, Alisa Hulsbosch, Carla E M Hollak, Christine Leopold, Aukje K Mantel-Teeuwisse, Wim G Goettsch
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundReimbursing orphan medicinal products (OMPs) presents both opportunities and challenges for national healthcare payers and health technology assessment (HTA) bodies because of their potential high benefits, large clinical uncertainties and high prices.

title: Reconfigurable Nonlinear Activation Using Low‐Loss Ge3Sb2Te15 for Photonic Neural Networks
creator: Yida Dong, Zhuoxuan Zhu, Yifan Zhu, Lichong Zhao, Lei Lei, Zihan Geng, Yida Li, X.‐D. Xiang, Heshan Yu, Mei Shen
description: The escalating demand for high‐performance computing has spurred interest in integrated silicon photonics to overcome the constraints of traditional von Neumann architectures. Reconfigurable photonic devices with low optical loss, high‐speed switching, and nonvolatile operation are essential especially for photonic neural networks.

title: Prostatic and scrotal necrosis following prostate artery embolization: a rare complication with a successful long-term outcome
creator: Aleksejs Zolovkins, Edoardo Massaro, Nicolò Ubaldi, Francesco Siciliano, Miltiadis Krokidis, Riccardo Lombardo, Tommaso Rossi, Marcello Andrea Tipaldi
description: BackgroundThis case report highlights a rare but severe complication of prostate artery embolization (PAE)—prostate necrosis. Once successfully managed, it resulted in an optimal long-term clinical outcome.Case presentationA 70-year-old male was diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and presented with severe lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), requiring a permanent urethral catheter.

title: Assessment of the trueness of the tissue surface for 3D-printed and injection-molded mandibular complete denture base fabrication
creator: Kai Li, Yanfang Zhao, Lin Ai, Huan Liu, Haitao Xin, Yan Zhang, Yulu Wu
description: BackgroundAs digital methods are widely used in clinical dentistry, the accuracy of dental prostheses remains critical. However, how each step in both conventional and digital methods affects the accuracy of the overall area and each area of the tissue surface remains unclear.

title: Elevated Galvanic Skin Response and Associated Brain Network Patterns in Youth at High Familial Risk for Bipolar Disorder
creator: Lisha Zhang, Kun Qin, Corey R Jones, L Rodrigo Patino, Nanfang Pan, Ziyu Zhu, Haoran Xu, Thomas J Blom, Jeffrey R Strawn, Qiyong Gong, Manpreet K Singh, Melissa P DelBello
description: ObjectiveAutonomic nervous system (ANS) dysfunction may be a key neuropathological feature of bipolar disorder. There is limited understanding of how perturbations in the ANS manifest and their relation to brain function in youth with a familial risk for bipolar disorder.

title: Endodontic microsurgery utilizing an autonomous robotic system for the maxillary second molar: a case report
creator: Minting Wan, Lishan Huang, Xiaoxing Li, Siyu Li, Qingsong Wu, Chengji Gong, Yufei Li, Xuechao Yang
description: BackgroundEndodontic microsurgery (EMS) is a widely utilized technique for addressing periapical periodontitis that is unresponsive to conventional root canal treatment. Nevertheless, achieving precise root apex location and resection can pose significant challenges for surgeons, particularly in complex anatomical situations. The inherent difficulties in accessing and the restricted visualization typically render EMS infeasible in the second molar region.

title: Space‐Time‐Coding Metasurfaces Enabling Programmable Range‐Angle‐Dependent Energy Auto‐Scanning
creator: Yuzhen Chen, Xiaoyi Wang, Guo‐Min Yang, Ya‐Qiu Jin
description: Dynamic regulation of electromagnetic energy distribution in space plays a pivotal role in fields like radar detection and wireless communications. However, the state‐of‐the‐art solution based on antenna array requires transmit/receive (T/R) modules per radiating element, causing exponential cost scaling and high power consumption.

title: Byte into sustainability: a scoping review of digital food environment attributes that shape consumers’ sustainability perceptions, attitudes, intentions, and behaviours
creator: Hannah Boen, Louise Glenisson, Lotte Hallez, Tim Smits
description: BackgroundCurrent food systems harm both planetary and human health. Meanwhile, our food choices are increasingly influenced by the digital food environment: spaces where digital actors (such as influencers) engage in food-related activities (like sharing content) across various platforms (for example, on social media).

title: High‐Order Janus Bound States in the Continuum Assisted by Unidirectional Guided Resonances
creator: Zengping Su, Jue Li, Haoye Qin, Wenjing Lv, Yongkang Wang, Wei Li, Linhan Lin, Bo Li, Qinghua Song
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Existing realizations of Janus bound states in the continuum (BICs) rely primarily on manipulating polarization singularities derived from accidental BICs. Here, we introduce a distinct strategy to engineer high‐order Janus BICs by leveraging interband‐coupling‐induced unidirectional guided resonances (UGRs). By breaking the out‐of‐plane symmetry in a square‐lattice photonic crystal slab, we manipulate the momentum‐space evolution of UGRs, driving them to coalesce with an intrinsic symmetry‐protected BIC at the Brillouin zone center.

title: Self-reported physical activity and risk of primary knee replacement for osteoarthritis: a competing risks cohort analysis
creator: Hao Peng, Qianying Cai, Dongning Liu, Vicky Duong, Win Min Oo, Changqing Zhang, David J Hunter, Yongqiang Zheng, Kai Fu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundWhether baseline self‑reported physical activity (PA) is associated with the risk of primary knee replacement (KR) for osteoarthritis (OA) remains uncertain, particularly across radiographic severity.MethodsIn 2,534 Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) participants with radiographic knee OA (RKOA; Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) ≥ 2) who completed the Physical Activity Scale for the Elderly (PASE) at baseline, we examined the association between PASE tertiles (low, moderate, high) and OA‑related primary KR over 108 months.

title: Fully Polarimetric Radar Cross‐Section and High‐Resolution Range Profile Co‐Modulation via Diversely Time‐Modulated Metasurface
creator: Hantao Xu, Jinxing Guo, Xinyang Mao, Shijian Yu, Yihao Xu, Peng You, Bin Zheng, Dongfang Guan, Zhen Liu, Yongxiang Liu
description: Advanced polarimetric radar systems, capable of capturing the full scattering matrix of targets, present significant challenges to electronic countermeasures (ECM). Although programmable metasurfaces offer a platform for electromagnetic manipulation, existing designs struggle to achieve simultaneous, diverse control over fully polarimetric radar cross section (RCS) and high‐resolution range profile (HRRP).

title: Establishing key components of a combined ayurvedic diet and yoga therapy program for weight management in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a Delphi study
creator: Vibhuti Rao, Mike Armour, Jennifer Rioux, Birinder S. Cheema, Alison Maunder, Caroline A. Smith, Carolyn Ee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundWomen with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) use Ayurveda and yoga to manage the symptoms, including excess weight. However, heterogeneity in the components of clinical trials limits the quality of current evidence in this area.

title: Modulation of NF-κB, MMP-1, and HAase by Coriandrum sativum Seed Extract in UV-Induced Skin Aging Model
creator: Meilinah Hidayat, Wahyu Widowati, Mariska Elisabeth, Anindita Putri Distya, Hanna Sari Widya Kusuma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Coriandrum sativum L. (coriander) contains abundant flavonoids and phenolic compounds that contribute substantially to its antioxidant capacity. These constituents exhibit strong free radical–scavenging activity, offering protection against cellular damage and premature skin aging, particularly under Ultraviolet (UV) exposure. This study evaluated the anti-aging effects of Coriander Seed Extract (CSE) in an in vitro UVB-induced photoaging model using human dermal fibroblasts (BJ cells).Methods:CSE was prepared through ethanol maceration. Cytotoxicity was assessed using the WST-8 assay.

title: Effects of iron replacement on electrocardiogram parameters in breath-holding spells patients with iron deficiency
creator: Gamze Aslan, Fatos Alkan, Onur Bircan, Senol Coskun
description: This study aimed to examine electrocardiogram parameters in patients with breath-holding spells accompanied by iron deficiency before iron treatment and after three months of iron supplementation therapy. A total of 195 children were included in the study, consisting of 95 patients with breath-holding spells and 100 age- and gender-matched controls. Patients were evaluated for iron deficiency at admission.

title: Engineered Extracellular Vesicles for Cartilage Regeneration: Bridging Biological Complexity to Clinical Precision
creator: Shayan Boozarjomehri Amnieh, Sina Mahmoudian, Mahdi Ghorbani, Javad Behroozi, Ali Shakerimoghaddam, Seyyed Morteza Tabatabaei, Zahra Hami, Mohsen Chamanara, Reza Heidari
description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disease characterized by pain, stiffness, progressive cartilage loss, and reduced mobility. Current treatments primarily aim to relieve symptoms rather than restore damaged cartilage, and durable regeneration of native hyaline cartilage remains a major clinical challenge.

title: Extended-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing Gram-negative bacteria are associated with high mortality in children with bloodstream infections in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
creator: Sabrina J Moyo, Joel Manyahi, Said Aboud, Kristine Mørch, Adam P Roberts, Bjørn Blomberg, Nina Langeland
description: ObjectivesStudies from Tanzania show rising prevalence of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) amongst key bacterial pathogens. We aimed to look at the clinical impact of bloodstream infections (BSI) caused by ESBL producing Gram-negative bacteria (GNB). This study was carried out on hospitalised children aged less than five years from four hospitals of the region of Dar es Salaam.

title: Diagnostic performance of adenosine deaminase activity in pleural fluid in tuberculous pleural effusion and relevant factors: a single-center experience with 1,491 consecutive patients
creator: Chi Yang, Xiang Shi, Shaojun Zhang, Mengting Xiong, Haili Hu, Xiaohui Hao, Wei Sha
description: ObjectiveAdenosine deaminase (ADA) is a widely-used diagnostic test for tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE), but its accuracy, optimal diagnostic threshold and relevant factors are controversial or unclear. We aimed to reassess these diagnostic variables in a large single center series.MethodThis retrospective study included 1,491 TPE patients and 597 malignant pleural effusion patients seen between 2012 and 2019.

title: Electrospun Poly Vinyl Alcohol-Chitosan Fiber Containing Punica Granatum: Promising Effects on Malignant Melanoma Cell Line
creator: Hamed Alipour, Maryam Aghdaki
description: Background:Melanoma is the deadliest type of cancer affecting the skin’s deeper layers and spreading rapidly to other tissues. The use of biodegradable scaffolding is widely used nowadays.Methods:In this study the anticancer activity against Malignant Melanoma (MM) of different concentrations of Punica granatum (PG) extract loaded on electrospun Poly Vinyl Alcohol- Chitosan fiber was evaluated.

title: miR-103/107–Mediated Suppression of NKILA Enhances Oncogenic Behaviors in Human Lung Cancer Cells
creator: Davood Jafari, Hossein Naghiloo, Seyyed Shamsadin Athari, Farshid Noorbakhsh, Nima Rezaei
description: Background:Lung cancer remains a major global health burden, and conventional therapies often fail to meet clinical needs. Although non-coding RNAs are increasingly recognized as key regulators in cancer, the role of NKILA and its modulation by the miR-103/107 cluster in lung cancer growth and metastasis is not fully characterized.

title: Study on the dynamic changes in antinuclear antibody spectrum in SARS-CoV-2 infection: a retrospective analysis
creator: Jing Zheng, Ying Zhang, Jing Wang, Yijun Chen, Guangjun Zhu, Yufen Zheng, Haixi Yan, Jun Li, Bo Shen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPatients with COVID-19 often produce multiple autoantibodies that impact immune function. This study aimed to assess changes in immune status and correlation with SARS-CoV-2 infection by analyzing dynamic shifts in patients’ antinuclear antibody (ANA) profiles.MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on ANA data and clinical characteristics of 680 patients with novel coronavirus pneumonia admitted to Taizhou Enze Medical Center (Group) between December 7, 2022, and January 31, 2023.

title: Ancestry-associated social and genomic hallmarks linked with inferior outcome in elderly acute myeloid leukemia
creator: Lacey S Williams, Alexis Williams, Olivia Wilkins, Sarah Mudra, Paul Sackstein, Garret Diltz, Rachel Zemel, Divya Lakshmi Padmanabhan, Gary M Kupfer, Purnima Sravanti Teegaparavu, Kimberley Doucette, Catherine Lai, Martha Mims, Anne Renteria, Gustavo Rivero
description: Recent literature reports inferior outcomes for patients of African ancestry (AA) who develop acute myeloid leukemia (AML). We herein present a cohort of 396 patients with 116 patients of AA (29%) who show inferior survival outcomes for patients of African ancestry ≥ 60 years (p = 0.008).

title: Using Electrostatic Mapping to Understand PANI-MWCNTs’ NH3 Sensing
creator: Alessia Famengo, Carmen Marinela Mihailescu, Mihaela Savin, Alexandru Grigoroiu, Carmen Moldovan, Maria Losurdo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study investigates the electrostatic and electrochemical behavior of polyaniline (PANI) and its composite with amine-functionalized multi-walled carbon nanotubes (PANI/MWCNT–NH2) to elucidate the mechanisms governing ammonia (NH3) sensing. High-resolution atomic force microscopy (AFM) coupled with electrostatic force microscopy (EFM) demonstrates that pristine PANI forms granular macroaggregates with localized charge distribution, whereas MWCNT incorporation promotes worm-like percolative networks that enhance charge delocalization and conductivity.

title: Pre-pandemic disease trajectories and genetic insights into long COVID susceptibility
creator: Natalia Blay, Xavier Farré, Judith Garcia-Aymerich, Gemma Castaño-Vinyals, Manolis Kogevinas, Rafael de Cid
description: BackgroundLong COVID refers to the persistence of symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection. While individual comorbidities have been studied, the role of coexisting chronic conditions remains underexplored. This study investigates whether pre-pandemic disease trajectories—sequential patterns of chronic conditions—modify long COVID risk and symptom profiles and explores shared genetic susceptibility.MethodsWe analysed 8322 adult participants (58.

title: Prevalence and predictors of decisional conflict among older African Americans with advanced chronic kidney disease
creator: Tyrone C Hamler, Aloen L Townsend, Mirela Dobre, Anne Huml, Monique J Brown
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and ObjectivesDecisional conflict (DC), or uncertainty about health-related decisions, is common among individuals with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet little is known about its prevalence and predictors among older African Americans, a population disproportionately affected by CKD.

title: Global Burden of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in Older Adults and Its Causal Association With Body Mass Index
creator: Yajuan Fu, Baohong Wang, Fang Li, Xinmin Tian, Jiwei Gu, Yujing Gao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a severe cardiopulmonary disease associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. However, the global burden, future trajectory, and potentially modifiable risk factors for PAH among older adults remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to quantify the global burden and projected trends of PAH among adults aged ≥ 60 years and investigate the causal association between body mass index (BMI) and PAH risk using Mendelian randomization (MR).

title: Evaluation of the Effects of Increasing Standard Uncertainty on the Combined Uncertainties: Case of an IE2 5.5 kW Induction Motor
creator: Edoardo Fiorucci, Andrea Fioravanti, Simone Mari, Giovanni Bucci, Fabrizio Ciancetta, Alberto Prudenzi
description: Developing electric motors with higher efficiencies for energy savings and environmental protection is crucial. The efficiency of grid-connected induction motors can be measured using various approaches; the preferred method is the indirect approach, which evaluates the separate losses from the additional losses due to residual losses.

title: Social factors contributing to the development of chronic low back pain: a scoping review
creator: Yvan Sonjon, Annabelle Gonthier, Camille Lépingle, Jean-Baptiste Van der Henst, Karen T Reilly, Eric Chabanat
description: BackgroundResearch and clinical practice approaches to chronic low back pain (CLBP) have predominantly focused on biomedical and psychological aspects, often overlooking social influences. The biopsychosocial (BPS) model provides a theoretical framework for conceptualizing CLBP as the outcome of complex interactions between individuals and their environment, offering valuable insights into its progression and informing effective care strategies.

title: Effects of using auto flow factor function on hemodialysis efficacy in regular hemodialysis patients
creator: Said S A Khamis, Ahmed Ragheeb Tawfeek, Mohammed Fathy Ragab, Heba Kamal Abd elkhalk
description: BackgroundRecent HD systems have moved from pre-defined dialysate flow rates (e.g. 300, 500, 800 mL/min) to an individual setting, or an automatic adjustment with a fixed factor of the dialysate flow to the blood flow. Both allows more flexibility of choosing the appropriate dialysate flow as an optimal adjustment to the current blood flow.

title: Voluntary assisted dying for dementia: international regulatory approaches and practices
creator: Casey M Haining, Lindy Willmott, Katrine Del Villar, Ben P White
description: An increasing number of jurisdictions now permit people to access voluntary assisted dying (VAD) to end their lives. Access to VAD is controlled by eligibility criteria, which vary in each jurisdiction meaning that not everyone who may wish to access VAD can.

title: Development and validation of the birth integrity questionnaire for measuring attitudes, maternity care, and perceptions of birth
creator: Stephanie Batram-Zantvoort, Céline Miani, Oliver Razum, Manuel Batram
description: BackgroundPublic health research on maternal health has increasingly focused on care quality, emphasizing subjective evaluations and addressing issues such as obstetric violence and mistreatment during childbirth. In 2014, the WHO called for research to prevent and eliminate mistreatment, advocating for respectful maternity care. While significant research exists in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, research in European settings is lacking.

title: Study of plasma exosomal miRNAs as novel biomarkers for differentiating primary central nervous system lymphoma and glioblastoma
creator: Shan Lu, Lixia Xu, Yu Lan, Chen Wang, Lidong Mo, Hua Yan
description: Preoperative diagnosis of the nature of PCNSL is crucial for distinguishing it from commonly confused intracranial gliomas, such as glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). The present research aims to sequence peripheral blood exosomal miRNAs from PCNSL and GBM patients, and to identify the discriminative miRNAs with high feasibility. Plasma exosomal RNAs were extracted, and miRNA sequencing was performed.

title: Long-term safety and efficacy of darvadstrocel for complex perianal fistulas in Japanese adults with Crohn’s disease: 3-year follow-up results
creator: Tsunekazu Mizushima, Satomi Furukawa, Rikisaburo Sahara, Akihiko Ohta, Yoshiki Okita, Takahiro Ito, Hiroki Ikeuchi, Daijiro Higashi, Akira Sugita, Kenichi Takahashi, Takayuki Ogino, Shigeru Kiryu, Ryo Nakaya, Nobuhiro Narii, Takayoshi Yamaguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Kitaro Futami
description: Background/AimsDarvadstrocel is a 1-time local injection for treatment-refractory complex perianal fistulas in patients with Crohn’s disease. Here we present 3-year (week 156) follow-up results from a Japanese phase 3, multicenter, open-label study of darvadstrocel.MethodsAdult Japanese patients with Crohn’s disease and complex perianal fistulas refractory to previous treatment were treated with darvadstrocel after fistula curettage and seton placement.

title: Clinical characteristics and prognostic analysis of concurrent Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in patients with malignancies: a retrospective study
creator: Yujie Shi, Ruxuan Chen, Kai Xu, Chi Shao, Yongjian Liu, Hui Huang
description: BackgroundPneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is a fatal opportunistic infectious disease. We conducted this study to describe the clinical characteristics and explore the prognostic factors of patients with concurrent malignancies and PJP (malignancy-PJP).MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled consecutive patients with malignancies diagnosed with PJP in our center from January 2014 to December 2022.

title: Historicising the prohibition of vulval cutting in the UK: how race and medicine shaped the criminalization of female genital mutilation
creator: Mireia Garcés de Marcilla
description: This article is a historical analysis of the law governing vulval cutting in the UK, with a particular focus on the shifting role and perception of the medical profession in this context. It shows how criminalization is not neutral or inevitable, but a strategy that developed through historically contingent negotiations between law and medicine.

title: Proteomics analysis of nitrogen stress on the influence of carbon and nitrogen metabolism of flue-cured tobacco
creator: Xinwang Zhang, Shouhui Pan, Dong Chen, Yuqi Pan, Tianju Xu, Jinling Zhang, Yin Huang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Nitrogen stress is the main abiotic stress factor affecting the carbon and nitrogen balance of flue-cured tobacco. Using tandem mass tag (TMT) proteomics, we identified 157 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) under low nitrogen (LN, 60 kg/hm2; 65 with increased abundance, 92 with decreased abundance) and 219 DEPs under high nitrogen (HN, 150 kg/hm2; 123 with increased abundance, 96 with decreased abundance).

title: 脑衰老进程中cGAS-STING信号通路介导炎症维持的机制及靶向干预
creator: Haoyue ZHANG, Danqi YU, Pinglong XU, Qirou WU, 敏 沈, 方 余
description: 脑衰老是多种神经退行性变性疾病发生发展的重要风险因素，其核心特征之一是慢性神经炎症。天然免疫cGAS-STING信号通路作为感知内源性损伤的关键传感器，是连接细胞衰老与慢性炎症的枢纽。在脑衰老进程中，核基因组损伤和线粒体功能障碍等导致异常的双链DNA进入细胞质，结合转座子异常活化及细胞间环鸟苷酸-腺苷酸传递等因素，共同驱动cGAS-STING信号通路持续活化。这不仅诱导下游干扰素及炎症因子的转录，而且通过重塑神经细胞生理功能加速脑功能衰退，表现为驱动胶质细胞向促炎表型转化并产生衰老相关分泌表型；诱导神经元细胞应激和死亡，导致突触稳态失衡及特定神经元亚群丢失。鉴于此，靶向cGAS-STING信号通路已成为延缓脑衰老的潜在策略。本文系统阐述脑衰老进程中cGAS-STING信号通路的激活机制，重点解析其在不同神经细胞中介导并维持炎症反应和功能重塑的分子机制，并探讨其在年龄相关神经退行性变性疾病中的作用及干预策略，旨在为阻断脑衰老相关的炎症级联反应提供理论依据和新视角。Keywords: 衰老, cGAS-STING信号通路, 天然免疫, 神经炎症, 综述 大脑作为稳态调节的中枢，其生物学年龄是预测多种神经退行性变性疾病的风险指标之一［1］。因此，解析大脑这一长寿关键器官的衰老机制，对于实现健康老龄化至关重要［2］。脑衰老不仅表现为认知功能进行性减退，更是多种分子和细胞损伤逐渐积累的过程［3］。从病理机制上看，衰老细胞积聚和天然免疫信号介导的慢性炎症微环境是脑衰老进程中重要的病理特征［4］。即便缺乏外源性刺激，衰老的中枢神经系统仍表现出持续的炎症因子水平升高［5-6］。在此背景下，小胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞向促炎表型转化，在分泌炎症因子的同时，对异常蛋白质聚集体的清除能力显著受损［7］。这种自我维持的炎症微环境对海马、前额叶皮质等氧化应激敏感脑区造成持续损伤，诱发神经元功能障碍，进而成为老年相关认知衰退及神经退行性变性疾病早期演变的关键驱动力［8］。 作为识别细胞质dsDNA的天然免疫信号，cGAS-STING信号通路在脑衰老慢性炎症机制研究中备受关注［9］。脑衰老进程中，细胞核及线粒体功能障碍导致损伤相关分子模式在细胞质中异常积累。这些异位遗传物质作为内源性配体，特异性激活cGAS-STING信号通路，尽管该信号通路在急性感染期具有防御意义，但在衰老微环境中其持续激活则促进神经炎症反应，并与神经元功能障碍密切相关［10-12］。研究显示，减少损伤相关分子模式或干预STING信号转导可减轻脑内炎症负荷并改善认知功能［13］，提示cGAS-STING信号通路不仅是脑衰老进程中炎症反应的启动因子，更是其长期维持的关键机制。基于此，本文回顾脑衰老进程中慢性炎症微环境形成和维持机制相关研究，重点阐述cGAS-STING信号通路的激活模式及其对不同神经细胞功能稳态的调控作用，并探讨靶向该通路的干预策略在延缓脑衰老进程中的潜在价值和临床转化前景。 脑衰老进程中的稳态失衡和炎症微环境 大脑因其高代谢需求、有限的再生能力以及对内环境稳态的高度依赖，易受慢性炎症、氧化应激、代谢紊乱等全身性衰老相关因素影响［14］。随着年龄增长，脑组织稳态逐渐失衡，表现为慢性炎症、突触丢失、脑室扩大、白质完整性降低及神经发生减少等病理改变，临床上表现为反应迟钝、记忆和理解能力减退、学习和协调能力衰退等认知功能障碍［15］。研究表明，脑衰老并非单一细胞类型病变，而是多种神经细胞获得衰老相关表型后协同驱动的结果［16］。尽管成熟神经元属于终末分化细胞，但在衰老或长期应激的病理条件下仍可表现出衰老相关的功能障碍，这也是多种神经退行性变性疾病的标志性事件［17］。同时，中枢神经系统中数量最丰富的星形胶质细胞会呈现衰老相关β-半乳糖苷酶活性升高、p16和p21表达上调，以及分泌衰老相关分泌表型等特征，导致其对神经元的支持和分隔功能受损［18］。而作为固有免疫细胞的小胶质细胞在衰老后转化为吞噬功能受损的促炎状态，驱动神经炎症产生［19-20］。此外，少突胶质细胞及其前体细胞因增殖能力下降，影响髓鞘的维持和修复［21］。构成血脑屏障的血管内壁细胞衰老则会破坏屏障完整性，促进外周炎症因子入脑，加剧神经炎症［22］。上述多种细胞的功能障碍共同构建了脑衰老进程中复杂的慢性炎症微环境。 在这些炎症微环境中，炎症因子的分泌和旁分泌作用构成了驱动神经炎症级联反应的分子基础［23］。外周循环中升高的IL-6不仅破坏血脑屏障完整性，还影响神经可塑性［24］，其诱导产生的C反应蛋白持续高表达与左侧旁海马回等脑区灰质萎缩有关［25-26］。外周炎症状态还可通过炎症因子及血脑屏障途径影响中枢神经系统：肿瘤坏死因子α作为炎症级联反应的核心放大器诱导细胞凋亡并促进β淀粉样蛋白等沉积［27］；IL-1β高表达则抑制海马区的长时程增强，干扰记忆巩固过程［28］。此外，CCL11等趋化因子参与外周和中枢的炎症通信，其血浆水平与认知状态呈负相关［29］。上述炎症因子与脑衰老进程中的稳态失衡等过程互相调控，最终形成持续的慢性低度神经炎症［30］。因此，慢性炎症不仅是脑衰老的重要特征，更是驱动衰老相关神经功能下降的重要因素。 cGAS-STING信号通路诱导神经炎症发生和维持 研究证明，cGAS-STING信号通路感知损伤相关分子模式并调节神经炎症，在脑衰老进程中扮演重要角色［31］。随着年龄增长，神经细胞中的基因组稳定性下降，ATM和ATR介导的损伤识别及同源重组修复介导的断裂修复等关键DNA修复机制受到限制，导致基因组损伤不断累积［32］。同时，细胞衰老过程中的关键结构蛋白质核纤层蛋白B1表达减少，增加了核膜通透性，不仅导致微核或染色质片段释放至细胞质被cGAS识别［33］，也使得细胞质中的cGAS更易穿过受损核膜，与核内暴露的染色质结合而活化［34］。此外，内源性逆转录病毒等逆转录元件活化后驱动了逆转录转座子的异常活化，这一现象已在老年食蟹猴海马组织中得到证实［35］。由此产生的逆转录产物在细胞质形成互补DNA积累，持续诱导cGAS-STING信号通路活化［36-37］。 除核基因组损伤外，线粒体功能障碍是驱动衰老相关天然免疫信号活化的另一关键因素。线粒体损伤或功能障碍会破坏其内膜完整性，改变膜通透性，促使游离mtDNA在膜电位失衡及线粒体基质肿胀的情况下释放至细胞质［38］。这一现象随年龄增长而加剧，研究证实老龄小鼠脑细胞中mtDNA水平显著高于年轻个体［12］。细胞质mtDNA积累也与氧化应激密切相关。机体老化伴随内源性抗氧化系统功能衰退，导致活性氧在组织中过度积累［39］。同时，自由基清除剂如褪黑素的浓度随年龄增长呈下降趋势，加剧线粒体损伤［40］。此外，线粒体转录因子A在脑组织衰老过程中表达下调以及Parkin和PINK1介导的线粒体自噬受损导致异常线粒体难以及时清除，加剧mtDNA突变和氧化损伤［41-42］。 除细胞内信号激活外，cGAMP还可以作为重要的第二信使在邻近细胞中传递，扩大衰老信号并促进相关炎症损伤［43］。例如，脑转移癌细胞通过Cx43缝隙连接与星形胶质细胞建立联系，将cGAMP转移至星形胶质细胞［44］。活化的星形胶质细胞表现出神经毒性特征，可分泌导致神经元死亡的有害介质［45］。神经元则可通过容积调节阴离子通道将cGAMP传递给小胶质细胞，接收到cGAMP信号的小胶质细胞触发Ⅰ型干扰素反应，放大神经炎症，而容积调节阴离子通道抑制剂Endovion则可减轻小胶质细胞激活及神经元凋亡［44］。mtDNA同样可以通过细胞外囊泡等途径进行细胞间传递，神经元来源的外泌体、微囊泡和凋亡小体可携带mtDNA，被小胶质细胞摄取后激活其中的cGAS。这类外源性mtDNA片段被称为循环游离mtDNA，其浓度随年龄增长而升高［46］。上述研究提示，cGAS-STING信号通路的信号分子能够通过细胞间传播进一步放大脑衰老过程中的炎症反应。值得注意的是，脑衰老进程也受到外周系统性炎症的影响。心血管老化和代谢紊乱可损害脑血管功能及血脑屏障完整性，加速外周炎症信号向中枢传播［47］。年龄相关睡眠结构和昼夜节律改变以及慢性睡眠不足均可削弱脑内代谢废物清除能力，加剧氧化损伤和炎症反应，加速脑衰老进程［48］。 与年轻小鼠比较，老年小鼠脑组织中cGAMP水平显著升高，提示cGAS在脑衰老进程中处于激活状态［31］。在老年非人灵长类动物及人类的前额叶皮质中同样观察到cGAS活性增强，伴随核因子κB及其下游促炎性细胞因子表达显著上调［49］。更为直接的证据是小鼠和人类的老年脑组织中cGAS与dsDNA结合事件增加，伴随海马小胶质细胞中Ⅰ型干扰素相关炎症标志物水平同步提升［12］。cGAS-STING信号通路的活化启动了炎症因子和趋化因子转录，促进衰老相关分泌表型形成并诱导细胞衰老［50］，而衰老细胞通过cGAMP非依赖途径诱导STING介导的无菌性炎症导致细胞由短暂免疫应答转变为持续性炎症状态［51］。综上，从细胞内损伤DNA持续累积到细胞间信号传递，这些多维度的病理改变共同反映cGAS-STING信号通路不仅启动神经炎症的级联反应，而且维持中枢神经系统慢性炎症微环境（图1）。 脑衰老中cGAS-STING信号通路活化机制及其介导的免疫应答示意图 在衰老的脑组织中，多种内源性核酸物质在神经细胞的细胞质中异常累积，主要源于基因组失衡导致的DNA片段或微核泄漏、线粒体功能障碍引起的线粒体DNA释放、逆转录转座子活化产生的互补DNA，以及细胞外囊泡介导的cGAMP或dsDNA在细胞间的传递；cGAS感知这些dsDNA后合成第二信使cGAMP，进而激活定位于内质网上的STING蛋白；活化的STING蛋白构象发生改变，从内质网转位到高尔基体，募集TBK1活化转录因子IRF3和NF-κB，诱导其核转位，最终驱动Ⅰ型干扰素和促炎性细胞因子表达. cGAS：环鸟苷酸-腺苷酸合成酶；STING：干扰素基因刺激因子；cGAMP：环鸟苷酸-腺苷酸；dsDNA：双链脱氧核糖核酸；TBK1：TANK结合激酶1；IRF3：干扰素调节因子3；NF-κB：核因子κB；IκB：核因子κB抑制蛋白. cGAS-STING信号通路介导脑衰老相关功能障碍 在脑衰老过程中，cGAS-STING信号通路异常活化影响了不同神经细胞的功能，进而介导中枢神经系统微环境失衡［52］。衰老脑组织中的小胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞异常聚集，因细胞内mtDNA积累激活cGAS-STING信号通路，逐渐转为促炎表型［53］。抑制STING可显著缓解老年中枢神经系统的炎症反应和神经退行性变［31］。在星形胶质细胞中激活的cGAS-STING信号通路通过转录因子YY1上调脂质运载蛋白2表达，促进衰老相关分泌表型分泌，加速衰老相关的微环境恶化［54］。与免疫细胞不同，稳态条件下成熟神经元中STING基础表达水平较低，并非经典的STING响应细胞［53］。然而，在脑损伤、慢性脑低灌注及溶酶体贮积症等病理状态下，神经元内STING蛋白水平显著升高并异常活化，诱导炎症因子释放、细胞应激反应以及神经元损伤，最终导致多巴胺能神经元丢失及脑功能障碍［55-58］。反之，cGAS-STING信号通路的功能性丧失能在一定程度上防止神经元丢失，改善认知和运动功能［59］。脑衰老作为年龄相关脑病的核心风险，通过诱导并放大神经细胞中dsDNA-cGAS-STING信号级联，将天然免疫监视转化为病理性神经炎症。 在脑衰老相关疾病中，蛋白质异常聚集往往通过诱导细胞应激、DNA损伤以及线粒体功能障碍等，成为驱动cGAS-STING活化的重要上游因素。在AD这种老年期最常见的痴呆症中，β淀粉样蛋白斑块周围的小胶质细胞中cGAS-STING信号通路活化增强，伴随干扰素调节因子3磷酸化水平升高以及Ⅰ型干扰素相关基因表达增加，表明该通路参与AD相关神经炎症维持［60］。在亨廷顿病中，突变型HTT异常聚集不仅破坏蛋白质稳态，还可通过诱导DNA损伤激活cGAS。亨廷顿病患者脑组织表现出显著的年龄相关衰老样特征，包括表观遗传年龄提前、外周血促炎性细胞因子水平升高、细胞应激耐受能力下降以及胶质细胞异常激活等［61］，这些衰老相关的改变加剧线粒体功能障碍，促进cGAS-STING信号通路活化，加剧神经元死亡和疾病进展［62］。亨廷顿病中cGAS缺失可抑制纹状体炎症基因表达及自噬［63］。在神经退行性运动障碍疾病帕金森病中，异常聚集的α突触核蛋白可通过磷酸化、羧基端截短及寡聚化等形式诱发线粒体功能障碍，间接促进mtDNA释放至细胞质，进而激活cGAS-STING信号通路［64］，并参与黑质、蓝斑、迷走神经背核、嗅球、大脑皮质等多个脑区的神经退行性病理过程［65-66］。在帕金森病模型中，神经元中STING持续活化能够促进细胞死亡，如在小鼠神经元中表达持续激活型STING突变体N153S将导致多巴胺能神经元丢失及运动功能障碍［55-58］。同样在帕金森病中，星形胶质细胞STING表达上调，特异性敲低cGAS表达或缺失干扰素受体均可减轻酪氨酸羟化酶阳性的多巴胺能神经元损伤，抑制衰老及神经退行性变［54］。在ALS中，由TARDBP基因编码的TAR DNA结合蛋白43在细胞质中异常聚集，引发线粒体功能障碍，并通过线粒体通透性转换孔促使mtDNA泄漏至细胞质，造成异常DNA信号积累，从而激活STING并损伤皮质中的神经元功能［67-68］。综上，cGAS-STING信号通路作为神经炎症的关键驱动力，通过整合多种衰老相关的细胞应激信号，在AD、亨廷顿病、帕金森病和ALS等多种神经退行性变性疾病中持续驱动中枢神经系统中的炎症微环境重塑和神经细胞功能障碍（图2）。 cGAS-STING信号通路在脑衰老相关功能障碍中的特异性激活机制 蛋白质异常聚集、沉积、功能异常等信号诱导cGAS-STING信号通路持续活化，参与年龄相关脑功能衰退过程. cGAS：环鸟苷酸-腺苷酸合成酶；STING：干扰素基因刺激因子；mHTT：突变型亨廷顿蛋白；TDP-43：TAR DNA结合蛋白43. 靶向cGAS-STING信号通路干预脑衰老进程 尽管诱导cGAS-STING信号通路激活的上游因素各异，但抑制STING的下游信号可有效减轻炎症反应并改善疾病相关表型，因此靶向cGAS-STING信号通路有望成为延缓年龄相关脑功能衰退的重要干预策略。 cGAS-STING信号通路抑制剂可以分为多种类型（表1）［69-85］。靶向cGAS的小分子药物主要阻断其与DNA结合或抑制催化活性，如抗疟药羟氯喹、衍生物X6、A151以及XQ2B竞争性结合cGAS，RU.521、G150及TDI-6570等小分子结合cGAS的催化结构域以减少cGAMP产生。STING抑制剂包括与STING的Cys91残基作用抑制其棕榈酰化的吲哚脲类H-151和硝基呋喃衍生物C-176，以及竞争性阻断cGAMP结合的SN-011和Compound
