title: BEATSCORE: Beat-Synchronous Contrastive Alignment and Event-Centric Grading for Long-Term Sports Assessment
creator: Lijie Wang, Jianyong Zhu, Houlei Wang, Xiaochao Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Long-term sports assessment is a challenging task in video understanding, since it requires judging subtle movement variations over minutes and evaluating action–music coordination. However, in many sporting events the background music is only weakly related to the performed movements, and the cues that matter for synchrony are often temporal and structural, such as small phase or tempo deviations that occur around decisive moments, rather than semantic correspondences between audio content and action categories.

title: The effect of kinesiophobia and successful aging on quality of life in older adults: machine learning approach
creator: Muhammet Ali Aydin, Nilufer Yildirim, Veysel Kizilarslan, Muruvvet Emrem, Şevin Polat, Metin YILDIZ
description: BackgroundKinesiophobia and successful aging are key factors affecting quality of life in older adults; kinesiophobia, the fear of movement, can lead to reduced physical activity, while successful aging promotes overall well-being.AimThis study was conducted to examine the effect of kinesiophobia and successful aging on quality of life in the older adults.

title: Episodic Future Thinking: A Behavioral Intervention to Promote Weight Loss in Breast Cancer Survivors (Alliance A21-Pilot10)
creator: Jasmine S. Sukumar, Maryam B. Lustberg, Jeffrey Stein, Patrick M. Schnell, Jenna King, Denise Schimming, Rachee Hatfield, Dionisia Quiroga, Ashley Davenport, Margaret E. Gatti-Mays, Nicole O. Williams, Mathew A. Cherian, Daniel G. Stover, Robert Wesolowski, Karen M. Basen-Engquist, Jennifer Vaughn,
description: PURPOSEObesity in breast cancer survivors (BCS) increases mortality, but lifestyle interventions have mixed outcomes. Episodic future thinking (EFT), in which individuals mentally simulate positive personal future-oriented events, has shown to reduce body weight (BW) and delay discounting (DD; the tendency to value delayed rewards less). How EFT affects BW reductions in BCS is unknown.

title: A systematic review of prediction models for risk of breast cancer
creator: Federica Re, Natnicha Manaboriboon, Iwan G. A. Raza, Alexandra Shipley, Lucy E. Thompson, Catherine Tiplady, Marina Blum, Gina Blum, Rumbidzai Mucheke, Roxanna E. Abhari, Christiana Kartsonaki
description: BackgroundPredicting the risk of breast cancer (BC) can help with early diagnosis, treatment, and prevention strategies. Existing BC risk prediction models typically utilize demographic, genetic, and/or imaging-derived variables. This systematic review summarizes all developed models for BC risk in general and high-risk populations, and their discriminatory ability and calibration.

title: Sex-specific shape models to disentangle sex effects and age-associated anatomical variation in biventricular cardiac anatomy
creator: Stefano Buoso, Valery L Visser, Pia Leuders, Tobias Kudelka, Maximilian Fuetterer, Christina Spengler, Robert Manka, Sebastian Kozerke
description: AimsAge- and sex-related differences in cardiac anatomy are well established using conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance biomarkers, but their representation in 3D ventricular shape remains unclear. In pooled statistical shape models, leading modes may be dominated by between-sex anatomical variation, potentially obscuring within-sex age-associated variation.

title: Effect of delayed cord clamping on the risk of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants with respiratory distress
creator: Jiajing Ge, Chenhong Wang, Huijia Lin, Guannan Bai, Yanping Xu, Liping Shi, Xiaolu Ma, Zheng Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeTo assess the incidence of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants born at < 32 weeks of gestation who received delayed cord clamping rather than early cord clamping.MethodsDuring this multicenter, prospective, observational cohort study, data of 1283 infants born at < 32 weeks of gestation who received umbilical cord management between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021, were collected from 26 tertiary referral neonatal intensive care units in China.

title: Genome-Wide Identification of the PLATZ Transcription Factor Family in Populus euphratica Oliv. and Functional Characterisation of PePLATZ8 in Drought Tolerance
creator: Tiantian Ran, Jianhao Sun, Chen Qiu, Xiaoli Han, Lijun Gao, Zhijun Li
description: Plant AT-rich sequence and zinc-binding (PLATZ) proteins are a class of plant-specific transcription factors that have been identified and functionally characterised in multiple species. However, the PLATZ gene family has not yet been systematically characterised in Populus euphratica. In this study, 19 PePLATZ genes were identified and classified into five subgroups.

title: APOE and amyloid‐tau pathology in cognitively unimpaired older adults
creator: Carlos Albarrán Morillo, Lukai Zheng, Elham Ghanbarian, Babak Khorsand, Crystal M. Glover, Joshua D. Grill, S. Ahmad Sajjadi, Ali Ezzati
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). INTRODUCTIONApolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype shows well‐established dose‐dependent associations with higher amyloid in cognitively unimpaired (CU) adults. In contrast, associations with tau burden and cognition are less well characterized.METHODSWe performed a cross‐sectional analysis of CU participants from the Anti‐Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease (A4), Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention (WRAP), and National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) within the harmonized multi‐cohort Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project Phenotype Harmonization Consortium (ADSP‐PHC) data.

title: BioSet2Vec: extraction of k-mer dictionaries from multiple sets of biological sequences via big data technologies
creator: Ylenia Galluzzo, Raffaele Giancarlo, Simona E. Rombo, Filippo Utro
description: BackgroundIn several contexts involving large collections of sets of biological sequences, a relevant problem is that of selecting significant groups of k-mers that characterize one set with regards to the others in the same collection.ResultsHere a software framework is proposed implementing a novel methodology for the extraction of k-mer dictionaries, from multiple sets of biological sequences.

title: Screening GGC repeat expansion in the NOTCH2NLC in early‐onset dementia: The Longitudinal Study of Early Onset Dementia and Family Members (LEAF) Study
creator: Seung‐yeon Lee, Takeshi Mizuguchi, Hee Jin Kim, Young‐Eun Kim, Cho Hanna, Won‐Joo Kim, Gha‐Hyun Lee, Ahro Kim, Ji‐Yun Park, Eun Joo Chung, Hyemin Jang, Na‐Yeon Jung, Sun Min Lee, Sang Won Seo, Seong‐Ho Koh, Henrik Zetterberg, Liana G. Apostolova, Naomichi Matsumoto, So Young Moon, Eun‐Joo Kim, the L
description: BACKGROUNDNeuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) is neurodegenerative disorder caused by GGC repeat expansion in NOTCH2NLC. Given its frequency in young East Asian adults and overlap with cognitive impairment in young adults, a key feature of early‐onset dementia (EOD), we screened NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansions in Korean patients with EOD.

title: From genome to gene expression: the genomic landscape of a hybrid species of Eucalyptus urophylla × Eucalyptus grandis and its divergence from parental species hybrid
creator: Guo Liu, Jianzhong Luo, Wanhong Lu, Yan Lin, Lei Zhang, Jingyi Pan, Jiangbo Zhai, Anying Huang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundEucalyptus urophylla × Eucalyptus grandis (E. urograndis) is a globally significant forest tree species renowned for its rapid growth, high yield, and exceptional wood production efficiency. A comparative analysis of its parental genomes, coupled with an in-depth investigation of the expression patterns of wood-related genes, will provide critical genomic resources to enhance research and utilization of this superior eucalypt hybrid species.ResultsIn this study, we present a draft genome assembly consisting of 592.09 Mb of data, with 99.91% anchored to 11 pseudochromosomes.

title: Influence of Mix Design Parameters on Fresh and Hardened Properties of Geopolymer Concrete: A State-of-the-Art Review
creator: Seemab Tayyab, Wahid Ferdous, Weena Lokuge, Tuan Ngo, Andreas Gerdes, Allan Manalo
description: Geopolymer concrete (GPC) has emerged as a promising low-carbon alternative to ordinary Portland cement (OPC), yet wider adoption is limited by the lack of standardised mix-design procedures. Precursor, activator, curing, and aggregates strongly interact to affect properties, but findings are scattered and hard to generalise.

title: Cultivation and mycelium production from spore suspensions of desert truffles: prospective use as inoculum for host plants in arid zones
creator: Kaddouri Hicham, Tounsi Abdessamad, Ouahmane Lahcen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Terfezia boudieri Chatin and Tirmania nivea (Desf.) Trappe, the desert truffles, are mycorrhizal fungi that are mostly endemic to arid and semi-arid areas of the Mediterranean where they are associated with Helianthemum species.

title: Severity and progression of visual impairment and risk of dementia
creator: Allen T C Lee, Owen N W Leung, Zhaohua Huo, Jessie O T Kwok, Kelvin K L Chong, Wai C Chan, Ada W T Fung, Suk L Ma, Ruby S Y Lee, Marcus Richards, Sheung‐Tak Cheng, Linda C W Lam
description: INTRODUCTIONVisual impairment is associated with dementia risk, but the role of severity and longitudinal change remains unclear. We examined whether visual impairment severity and its progression were associated with incident dementia.METHODSThis territory‐wide cohort study followed 15,576 community‐dwelling older adults without dementia at baseline for 16 years.

title: Fabrication of Magnetically and Photothermally Functionalized Materials Based on Corn Stalk Pith Framework for Oil–Water Separation
creator: Yutong Cui, Xin Shu, Boyu Cui, Jiayan Ding, Wei Dai, Chunmao Yang, Weihong Wang
description: To address critical challenges in marine oil spill remediation, including limited penetration of high-viscosity crude oil and inefficient adsorbent recovery, it is imperative to develop environmentally friendly materials integrating high-efficiency adsorption, in situ viscosity reduction, and controllable recovery. In this study, a delignified corn pith (CPDL) with a three-dimensional porous structure was employed as a green matrix.

title: Insulin Resistance and Beta Cell Function in Hepatogenous Diabetes
creator: Kirandeep Kaur, Anand Sharma, Gourab Bhaduri, Ch Jagapathi Babu, Aneesa A. Mirza, Yogesh Bahurupi, Kalyani Sridharan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction:The present study aimed to examine the change in beta cell function and insulin resistance (IR) over 6 months in patients with liver cirrhosis (LC) and hepatogenous diabetes (HD) and to assess their correlation with liver disease severity.Methods:One hundred and seventy-three patients with LC without a prior history/risk factors of type 2 diabetes mellitus and with non-diabetic fasting blood glucose and glycated haemoglobin were subjected to a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT).

title: Development and validation of an echocardiographic nomogram for identifying cardiac amyloidosis in patients with left ventricular hypertrophy
creator: Shichu Liang, Zhiyue Liu, Fanfan Shi, Liping Chen, Dayan Li, Ying Peng, Wenfeng He, Chaohui Du, He Huang
description: BackgroundEchocardiography is the principal non-invasive imaging modality for screening cardiac amyloidosis (CA). This study aimed to establish a cohort of CA-associated left ventricular hypertrophy (CA-LVH) within a hospital-based population and to develop an echocardiographic identification model for CA using readily available echocardiographic parameters.

title: Thiol-Functionalized Succinoglycan via Cysteine Grafting: Enhanced Rheological Properties and Antioxidant Activity
creator: Sobin Jeon, Kyungho Kim, Eunkyung Oh, Haemin Jin, Seunho Jung
description: Cysteine-modified succinoglycan (SG-Cys) was synthesized via EDC/NHS-mediated amidation by grafting cysteine onto succinoglycan isolated from Sinorhizobium meliloti. The successful introduction of cysteine moieties was confirmed by 1H NMR and FTIR analyses, while the degree of substitution was quantitatively determined using Ellman’s assay. The incorporation of cysteine significantly influenced the physicochemical and rheological properties of the polymer.

title: Diabetic Myonecrosis: An Under-Recognised Complication of Poorly Controlled Diabetes with a High Morbidity– A Clinico-Radiological Study
creator: Varun Kumar, Mohammed A. Hussain, Mathews E. Kurian, Neeraja Balan, Benjamin B. Mathew, Madhavi Kandagaddala, Harini S. Arumugam, Kripa E. Cherian, Nitin Kapoor, Hesarghatta S. Asha, Nihal Thomas, Felix Jebasingh
description: Introduction:Diabetic myonecrosis is an uncommon and under-recognised complication of diabetes mellitus. We aimed to describe the clinical profile, imaging characteristics, management strategies, and outcomes of patients with diabetic myonecrosis.Methods:This retrospective study included 30 patients diagnosed with diabetic myonecrosis between 2002 and 2024. Diagnosis – based on clinical suspicion, supported by characteristic ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging.

title: Impact of PG-SGA-assessed malnutrition stratification on clinical outcomes in advanced gastrointestinal malignancies: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Pei Zhuang, Jun-xuan Chen, Bing Xia, Xiao-su Chen, Xiao-tian Chen, Li Li, Ting Zhu, Shu-an Wang, Qing-yan Li
description: IntroductionThe traditional TNM staging system fails to explain survival heterogeneity in advanced gastrointestinal cancer, while malnutrition remains an underutilized prognostic modulator. We aimed to establish the prognostic value of dynamic nutritional risk stratification using the Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA).

title: Impact of Wild Edible Fruits of Arbutus unedo and Crataegus monogyna on Gut Motility, Contraction, Secretion, and Glucose Regulation
creator: Soumaya Wahabi, Kais Rtibi, Chaima Abidi, Mourad Jridi, Bernard Gressier, Hichem Sebai, Bruno Eto
description: BackgroundArbutus and hawthorn fruits are commonly utilized in traditional medicine to address various gastrointestinal (GI) ailments. Our primary aim was to individually assess the effects of aqueous extracts from Arbutus unedo (AUAE) and Crataegus monogyna (CMAE) fruits on GI motility, spontaneous jejunal smooth muscle contractility, and hyperglycemia management.MethodsWistar rats were administered loperamide (LOP, 3 mg/kg, b.w.

title: The Role of Long Non-Coding RNA in Atherosclerosis: Mechanism and Intervention of Traditional Chinese Medicine
creator: Dongmei Yang, Jingyue Wei, Wanjun Lin, Lingran Feng, Qinhui Tuo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Atherosclerosis (AS) is a cardiovascular disease characterized by diverse etiological factors and complex pathological mechanisms. In recent years, the role of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in AS has received increasing attention. Research shows that lncRNAs regulate key biological processes involved in AS, such as vascular endothelial function, proliferation and migration of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), macrophage polarization, and lipid metabolism, through various mechanisms, including epigenetic modification, transcriptional regulation, and post-transcriptional control.

title: Forgotten Gangliosides: O-Acetylated and Lactone Gangliosides
creator: Laura Mauri, Stefano Vaghi, Sandro Sonnino
description: Gangliosides containing O-acetyl-sialic acid or a sialic acid forming a lactone ring, classified as alkali-labile gangliosides (ALGs), were the focus of extensive research until the late 1990s. Their identification and isolation for structural characterization require strict avoidance of alkaline treatments, a common step in standard ganglioside purification protocols used to eliminate glycerophospholipid contamination.

title: Longitudinal measures of monkey brain structure and activity through adolescence predict cognitive maturation
creator: Junda Zhu, Clément M Garin, Xue-Lian Qi, Anna Machado, Zhengyang Wang, Suliann Ben Hamed, Terrence R Stanford, Emilio Salinas, Christopher T Whitlow, Adam W Anderson, Xin Maizie Zhou, Finnegan J Calabro, Beatriz Luna, Christos Constantinidis
description: In humans and other primates, adolescence is associated with improvement in cognitive abilities and with changes in brain structure and connectivity. However, how these changes affect neural activity underlying cognitive performance remains unknown. Here we conducted a multilevel, longitudinal study of monkey adolescent neurocognitive development by tracking behavior, neuronal activity and anatomical imaging measures.

title: Effects of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in patients with type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: A cohort study
creator: Rania Naguib, Nouran Aleyeidi, Hend Naguib
description: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) are a novel group of oral medications used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), a complication of T2DM, is now recognized as one of the most frequent causes of chronic liver disorders.

title: Synergistic optical, dielectric and visible-light photocatalytic enhancement in Mo-modified BaTiO3 nanostructures
creator: Mohammed Ahmed Wahba, Saad Mabrouk Yakout, A. M. Youssef
description: Molybdenum-doped barium titanate (BaTiO3) nanostructures were fabricated by a solid-state reaction and evaluated for simultaneous enhancement of dielectric and optical performance. X-ray diffraction confirmed that progressively higher Mo content drives a tetragonal to cubic phase transformation, evidencing effective lattice tuning. Complementary SEM and EDX analyses showed well-defined grain morphology and uniform elemental distribution, verifying successful Mo incorporation.

title: Does travel distance influence short‐term outcome after periacetabular osteotomy?—A cohort study
creator: Quentin Karisch, Chiara Heller, Justus Stamp, Marco Haertlé, Henning Windhagen, Sufian S. Ahmad
description: PurposePeriacetabular osteotomy (PAO) is an established joint‐preserving procedure for the treatment of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). As PAO is typically concentrated in specialized centres, many patients travel considerable distances for treatment. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the influence of travel distance on short‐term outcomes following PAO.

title: A peptide-based medical device for the selective removal of inflammatory factors from the blood of people with sepsis
creator: Giovanni Cappello, Laura Cresti, Clelia Cortese, Letizia Bocchi, Elena Bianchini, Filippo Carlucci, Marcello Fiorini, Jlenia Brunetti, Chiara Falciani, Luisa Bracci, Alessandro Pini
description: BackgroundSepsis is a complex life-threatening clinical condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality. It is usually triggered by an infection, the cellular response to which progresses, involving the innate immune system and leading to a cytokine storm that can provoke death.MethodsThe device is based on the peptide SET-M33, an antimicrobial molecule with strong antibacterial activity.

title: Spectroscopic quantification of cyclopentolate using an erythrosine-based resonance rayleigh scattering strategy: application to ophthalmic formulations
creator: Ahmed A. Abu-hassan
description: Cyclopentolate (CYP), an antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) agent, is pharmacologically employed in ophthalmology to induce cycloplegia (temporary paralysis of the ciliary muscle) and mydriasis (pupil dilation) for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, including ocular examinations and surgeries. This study establishes a spectrofluorimetric method for quantifying CYP in ophthalmic solutions based on Resonance Rayleigh Scattering (RRS) signal modulation.

title: Extracerebral microvascular burden links to dementia risk and brain structural changes: Evidence from a large‐scale cohort study
creator: Jialin Li, Yingzhe Wang, Chunyu Yin, Mei Cui, Jincheng Li, Chen Suo, Kelin Xu, Zhenqiu Liu, Li Jin, Xingdong Chen, Yanfeng Jiang
description: INTRODUCTIONThe contribution of extracerebral microvascular disease (MVD) burden to dementia risk remains unclear.METHODSAmong 484,896 UK Biobank participants (median follow‐up 8.5 years), baseline extracerebral MVD (retinopathy, nephropathy, peripheral neuropathy) and incident dementia were identified via hospital records. Aging‐related brain changes were evaluated using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) ‐derived volumes and white matter integrity.RESULTSMVD was 2.

title: A full life cycle biological clock based on routine clinical data and its impact in health and diseases
creator: Kai Wang, Fei Liu, Wei Wu, Changxi Hu, Xian Shen, Meihao Wang, Gen Li, Fanxin Zeng, Li Liu, Io Nam Wong, Sian Liu, Zixing Zou, Bingzhou Li, Jinghang Li, Xiaoying Huang, Shengwei Jin, Zhuomin Li, Hui Xu, Gang Chen, Xiaodong Chen, Ying Zhu, Ping Li, Zhe Feng, Winston Wang, Linling Cheng, Mingqi Yang,
description: Aging research has primarily focused on adult aging clocks, leaving a critical gap in understanding a biological clock across the full life cycle, particularly during infancy and childhood. Here we introduce LifeClock, a biological clock model that predicts biological age across all life stages using routine electronic health records and laboratory test data.

title: BLASE: bulk linkage analysis for single cell experiments - teasing out the secrets of bulk transcriptomics with trajectory analysis
creator: Andrew McCluskey, Toby Kettlewell, Adrian M. Smith, Rhiannon Kundu, David A. Gunn, Thomas D. Otto
description: BackgroundTranscriptomics has profoundly improved our knowledge of cells. The advent of single-cell transcriptomics has enabled researchers to investigate the changes which individual cells undergo, such as cell type differentiation. Bulk RNA-seq is more practical in both cost and ease, but cannot elucidate cell type specific trajectories.

title: Author Correction: Incidence of opioid-induced constipation in non-cancer patients using weak opioids for chronic pain in Japan: a cohort study
creator: Akira Hashimoto, Yasuhide Morioka, Shihomi Wada, Yuichi Koretaka, Motoki Sonohata

title: Exogenous neoagaro-oligosaccharides accelerate seed germination and alleviate the impact of growth retardants on germination and seedling growth of garden cosmos (Cosmos bipinnatus Cav.)
creator: Xinyao Yang, Chao Wen, Linfeng Gong, Hanting Zeng
description: Neoagaro-oligosaccharides (NAOS) are degraded seaweed polysaccharides of low molecular weight and high water solubility. Currently, little information is available on the utility of NAOS for seed germination. Here, we investigated seed germination of garden cosmos under NAOS concentrations of 0, 0.01, 0.

title: Arthroscopic Supraspinatus Tendon Reconstruction Using Hybrid LARS-Fascia Lata Graft for Irreparable Posterosuperior Massive Rotator Cuff Tears
creator: Xiaoli Gou, Zhenyu Wang, Xueyan Zhao, Xuping Tian, Binghua Zhou
description: Background:Conventional techniques for repairing an irreparable posterosuperior massive rotator cuff tear (MRCT) typically fail1,2. The supraspinatus tendon reconstruction (STR) technique offers a systematic approach to achieve both anatomic restoration and functional recovery of the supraspinatus tendon1. The use of autografts for reconstruction is challenged by their limited availability, inadequate dimensions, and donor site morbidity.

title: Delineating multiobjective ecological management zones and revealing scale effects of thresholds for factors influencing ecosystem services in Jiangxi Province
creator: Xuelong Yang, Jun Zhang, Haisheng Cai, Xiaomin Zhao, Han Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Elucidating the connection between the total supply and demand of ecosystem services (ESTSD) can provide comprehensive decision support for regional eco-management. Previous studies have focused on the spatial and temporal evolution of ESTSDs in the horizontal dimension but studies in the vertical dimension are lacking; too much attention has been given to single dimensions for ecological management zoning while omitting multilevel and multiobjective considerations; and there are limitations in knowledge about the threshold scale effect of ecosystem service (ES) influencing factors.

title: Out-of-Plane Skew Effects on the Cyclic Performance of Column-Tree Steel Moment Connections
creator: Geon-Woo Kim, Jong-Kook Hong
description: This study investigates the influence of out-of-plane beam skew on the cyclic performance of column-tree steel moment connections. Utilizing validated finite element (FE) models against experimental data, the cyclic responses of various configurations were evaluated under the AISC cyclic loading protocol up to a story drift ratio of 0.05 rad.

title: Intravenous Thrombolysis Prior to Endovascular Treatment in Basilar Artery Occlusions: A Patient Pooled Analysis of Four Randomized Controlled Trials
creator: Robrecht R M M Knapen, Mohamed F Doheim, Heinrich J Audebert, Francisco Mont’Alverne, Volker Pütz, Patrik Michel, Xinfeng Liu, Qiliang Dai, Wei Hu, Chunrong Tao, Rui Liu, Pengfei Xu, Chuanhui Li, Xunming Ji, Tudor G Jovin, Christiaan van der Leij, Robert J van Oostenbrugge, Wim H van Zwam, Raul G No
description: PurposeThis study assessed intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) prior to endovascular treatment (EVT) versus EVT alone in patients with basilar artery occlusions (BAO).MethodsThis patient-level pooled analysis included data from four randomized controlled trials within the VERITAS collaboration (BEST, BASICS, ATTENTION, and BAOCHE). Patients were stratified into IVT plus EVT and EVT alone.

title: Optimizing Dental Resin-Based Composite Polymerization with Distance and Exposure Variables: Preliminary Study
creator: Anna Lehmann, Bolesław Barszcz, Kacper Nijakowski
description: Resin-based composites (RBCs) are widely used in restorative dentistry, and their clinical performance depends on the degree of conversion (DC). Light-curing units are used to initiate polymerization, but factors such as the distance between the light source and the composite surface as well as different exposure modes can affect DC.

title: Multi-scenario simulation of land use change based on the objectives of cultivated land, ecological protection, and economic development in Yunnan Province, China
creator: Wenqi Tang, Jianqiang Li, Huiying Yan, Lianling Cha, Yuan Yang, Linling Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Land use change scenario simulation based on multi-objective synergy can provide a scientific basis for coordinating ecological protection, resource management and economic development by quantitatively analysing and predicting the dynamic evolution of land use. As an ecological security barrier and cross-border opening frontier in southwest China, Yunnan Province is characterised by “mountainous and cross-border” land use change, which poses a multidimensional challenge to the sustainable development of the region.

title: Enhancing the Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Effectiveness of a AZ61 Magnesium Alloy by Deformation and Subsequent Heat Treatment
creator: Minhyeok Kang, Kyengtaek Kim, Seongje Kim, Jose Victoria-Hernandez, Dietmar Letzig, Sangbong Yi
description: Highlights The increased dislocation density and deformation twins induced by hot rolling contribute to enhanced electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding effectiveness.During aging of the AZ61 alloy, precipitates preferentially form along the basal (0002) planes.The increased density of precipitates distributed along the basal (0002) planes contributes to improved electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding effectiveness.

title: Evaluation of CuS nanorods surface interaction with Cd2+ ions, Methyl Orange and microbes for clean water management
creator: R Lakshmipathy, S Radjarejesri, Venkatesa Prabhu Sundramurthy, Mohamed Abbas, Nagaraj Ashok
description: In this study, we report an eco-friendly approach for synthesizing CuS nanorods using aqueous extract of Syzygium cumini seeds as a sustainable alternative. The formation of CuS nanorods were confirmed with UV-Vis, SEM and TEM investigations and were found to be around 6–10 nm in length with hexagonal phase.

title: Academic anxiety and cognitive reflection in neurodivergence based on evidence from a large international sample
creator: Sheeza Mahak, Stephanie Malone, Mahmoud Elsherif, Christopher J. Hand, Kinga Morsanyi
description: Anxiety is commonly experienced by neurodivergent individuals participating in higher education, related to both cognitive performance and academic achievement. Whereas certain anxieties in neurodivergence (e.g., social and general anxiety) have received more attention, scant research has considered mathematics and statistics anxiety.

title: Effect of Dala‐Led Behavior Change Communication on Complementary Feeding Practices in Infants and Young Children: A Cluster‐Randomized Controlled Trial in Agro‐Pastoral Settings of Afar Region, Ethiopia
creator: Anwar Seid Ali, Tefera Belachew, Shemsu Kedir, Kalkidan Hassen Abate
description: Suboptimal complementary feeding remains a major public health concern in Ethiopia, particularly among pastoralist and agro‐pastoral communities where mobile livelihoods hinder access to conventional health services. In these settings, numerous studies have highlighted the potential of leveraging culturally embedded leadership structures to enhance health promotion efforts.

title: Community‐Based Interventions for Childhood Undernutrition in Sub‐Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Network Meta‐Analysis
creator: Francis P. Riwa, Mark A. Jones, Kazi Mizanur Rahman, Andrew A. Mushi, Kate Mueller
description: Childhood undernutrition remains a major public health challenge in sub‐Saharan Africa (SSA), despite global progress. This review evaluated the effectiveness of community‐based interventions for treating undernutrition among children aged 6–59 months in SSA. We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Cochrane CENTRAL from inception to August 2024, without language restrictions.

title: Multifunctional Dyeing Process and Characterization of Silk Fabric Based on Natural Colorant of Rhubarb
creator: Xuzhi Sun, Ge Pan, Xiaojuan Li, Qingru Huang, Xiang Ma, Mingfei Sheng, Maoli Yin
description: To promote the application of natural dyes in eco-textiles and develop multifunctional silk fabrics, this study optimized the extraction of functional pigments from rhubarb and investigated their dyeing performance and functional properties on silk. The optimal extraction conditions were determined as pH 11, 80 °C, 50 min, with three extraction stages.

title: Variable gradient-based phase locked loop for accurate frequency estimation of distorted grids
creator: Xiaoben Lei, Xinhua Hu, Jianwei Yang, Guangqi Li, Zhiyong Dai, Guoqing Wang
description: A variable gradient-based phase locked loop (VG-PLL) is developed for distorted grids. Firstly, the large-signal model of the synchronous reference frame phase locked loop (SRF-PLL) with harmonic disturbances is established, and the large-signal model shows that the SRF-PLL has poor filtering effects in estimating the grid frequency. To address this issue, a VG-PLL is then proposed.

title: Amino-Acid-Derived Toxins and Pyrazines in Chocolates and Cocoa-Free Chocolate Surrogates
creator: Alexandre Dusart, Lucie Villé, Thomas Vantsiotis, Sonia Collin
description: This study investigated the influence of cocoa-bean amino acid profile on the formation of α,β-unsaturated carbonyls. Some of these heat-derived compounds generated primarily during roasting (often through Strecker degradation and aldol condensation) are of toxicological concern (e.g., the aneugenic 2-phenylcrotonaldehyde and the genotoxic furan-2(5H)-one). Here, their levels were compared by SAFE-GC/MS in cocoa of different origins, before and after roasting.

title: Investigating the effect of task engagement during intertrial rest periods on micro offline gains
creator: Nafiz Ishtiaque Ahmed, Tharan Suresh, Sara J. Hussain, Michael Freedberg
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Explicit motor sequence learning (ESL) consolidation manifests as skill improvements during rest periods that last minutes or longer. However, recent evidence suggests that ESL improvements also occur during inter-trial rest periods that last seconds (micro offline gains; MOGS). While indirect evidence supports that MOGS is a phenomenon tied to brief periods of wakeful rest, this hypothesis has never been directly tested.

title: DUET: a graph-based workflow for TCR-epitope prioritization and tumor-reactive T-cell identification
creator: Yunsheng Chen, Vanessa Giuliano, Ian Dacillo, Wenjun Lin, Yan Yan, Ping Luo
description: Accurate prioritization of T-cell receptor (TCR)-epitope interactions and identification of tumor-reactive T cells are important but difficult steps in immunotherapy-oriented bioinformatics workflows. Existing methods typically address these tasks separately and either model TCR-epitope pairs as independent observations or rely primarily on transcriptomic signatures.

title: Development of an LC-MS/MS-Based Analytical Method, In Vitro Characterization, and Pharmacokinetic Study of Rafoxanide Nanosuspension in Sheep
creator: Kairui Sun, Bing Li, Fusheng Cheng, Yaxin Zhou, Guonian Dai, Haiquan Li, Ligang Yuan, Jiyu Zhang
description: Simple SummaryThis study aimed to establish a more sensitive and reliable quantitative detection method for rafoxanide in sheep plasma and apply it to an 84-day long-term pharmacokinetic study comparing a nanosuspension with a conventional suspension. The results showed that RFX-NS had a smaller particle size, a more uniform distribution, a higher Zeta potential, and better in vitro dissolution.

title: Association between aortic valve calcification and cardiovascular events in patients with chronic kidney disease
creator: Saki Hayashida, Naoki Haruyama, Hiroyuki Hayashida, Akiko Fukui, Osamu Ohta, Ryota Yoshitomi, Masaru Nakayama
description: The association between aortic valve calcification (AVC) and cardiovascular (CV) events across diverse populations including patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains controversial. This study aimed to determine whether AVC is associated with CV events in patients with CKD. In this prospective study, 1,279 participants with CKD were enrolled.

title: Association between the left-sided atrial septal pouch and the cryptogenic stroke – an updated systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Kamil Tyrak, Jakub Batko, Jakub Hołda, Kacper Jaśkiewicz, Mateusz Hołda
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Cryptogenic stroke, named embolic stroke of undetermined source, refers to patients for whom the etiology of embolism remains unknown. Recently a new cardiac entity, the left-sided septal pouch (LSSP), has been identified as a possible source of thromboembolic events. In the current study, we aimed to perform a systematic review of the literature on this topic and to determine the association between the LSSP presence and occurrence of cryptogenic stroke using meta-analytical methodologies.

title: Attentional variability as a cognitive marker of clinical activity in Crohn’s disease
creator: Andreza Maia, Juliana Janeiro Schmidt, Carlos Eduardo Brandão Mello, Guilherme Janeiro Schmidt, Yolanda Faia Manhães Tolentino, Márcia Maria Amendola Pires, Ana Caroliny da Silva, Julia Dias Guimarães Silva, Marcia Lyrio Sindorf, Sergio Luis Schmidt
description: BackgroundBehavioral and cognitive manifestations have been increasingly recognized in Crohn disease (CD), yet the specific behavioral domains associated with clinical activity remain incompletely characterized. Although reduced response speed has been proposed as a key feature, moment-to-moment fluctuations in performance may better capture behavioral instability related to systemic inflammation.

title: Infrared Thermography of Cattle Hooves: Temperature Differences According to Lameness Score
creator: Tina Bobić, Mihaela Oroz, Marko Oroz, Nikola Raguž, Pero Mijić, David Kranjac, Mario Shihabi, Emmanuel Karlo Nyarko, Stanko Horvat, Boris Lukić
description: Simple SummaryLameness represents a major problem on dairy farms, with significant implications for animal welfare and farm profitability. Timely detection of hoof diseases and the consequent prevention of lameness is, therefore, crucial. There are several methods available for detecting lameness in cows, and these can be broadly classified as direct (cow gait analysis, image-processing techniques, weight distribution platforms, etc.

title: NGH分类辅助下的夏科氏肩关节病影像学评估与治疗
creator: 骁然 孙, 雨晨 贺, 晓磊 任, 威宏 朱
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 夏科氏肩关节病是一种罕见的破坏性关节病，多继发于脊髓空洞症，常导致肩关节骨溶解与严重的上肢功能障碍。其诊疗难点不在于单纯识别关节破坏，而在于早期症状缺乏特异性，易与感染、肿瘤及炎症性关节病混淆；同时，肩胛盂与肱骨头骨破坏程度差异较大，传统的影像学描述难以为术前评估和治疗决策提供直接依据。NGH(neuropathic gleno-humeral degeneration)分类基于X线平片分别独立评估肩胛盂与肱骨头的退变程度，有助于减少影像描述的模糊性，为临床手术决策提供参考。现有证据提示，夏科氏肩关节病的临床处理应建立在综合评估的基础上：NGH分类辅助X线可用于初步诊断，磁共振成像(magnetic resonance imaging，MRI)可评价软组织等，CT+3D有助于骨缺损量化和假体规划；存在肿胀、积液、炎症指标升高或拟手术者，应结合关节穿刺、活检排除感染、肿瘤和炎症性疾病。对于关节破坏进入静止期的患者，可采取肩关节置换术等手术。未来仍需开展多中心、前瞻性队列研究及长期随访，以进一步验证NGH分类的临床价值，并明确肩关节置换术的长期疗效。

夏科氏肩关节病是一种因神经感觉缺陷而发生的慢性关节疾病[1-2]。其主要病因为脊髓空洞症(syringomyelia，SM)，其他病因包括梅毒、糖尿病及创伤等[3]。无痛性肿胀、关节活动度受限、肌力减弱等症状是该病的临床早期表现，中晚期可出现部分或全部感觉丧失、肩关节脱位及骨结构破坏等。

夏科氏肩关节病的临床处理目前面临多重困难。第一，早期症状不典型，患者容易被误诊为感染、肿瘤或炎症性关节病[1, 4-5]。第二，多数患者发现时已存在肱骨头和肩胛盂不同程度骨破坏，单纯使用“骨溶解严重”或“关节破坏明显”等描述难以指导后续影像评估和术前讨论。第三，由于夏科氏肩关节病发病率极低，且手术治疗证据主要来自病例报告，术式选择不能简单套用普通肩关节退变性疾病的治疗逻辑。

基于上述问题，本文介绍夏科氏肩关节病的主要发病机制、诊断路径及手术策略，重点聚焦NGH(neuropathic gleno-humeral degeneration)分类系统(该分类可根据影像学结果对不同损伤程度患者进行分层，独立评估肩胛盂与肱骨头的退变程度)辅助下的夏科氏肩关节病影像学评估与治疗，以期为临床诊断与综合治疗策略提供参考。

夏科氏肩关节病的流行病学特征与发病机制

流行病学特征

一项纳入39篇病例报告(共包含65例患者，71肩)的系统评价[6]显示，患者的发病年龄为(51.1±15.8)岁，女性略多于男性(女꞉男=1.2꞉1)。受累关节以单侧为主(90.8%)，左右两侧无显著差异，且绝大多数患者伴有关节活动度(range of motion，ROM)受限。27%的患者有创伤史，与无创伤史患者相比，诊断时间缩短69%[1]。

发病机制

夏科氏肩关节病是一种神经性关节病，多继发于SM。SM可继发于Arnold-Chiari等先天畸形，或由恶性肿瘤、脊髓损伤等因素引起[7]。Chiari Ⅰ畸形、SM和夏科氏肩关节病三者间的关系是临床上最主要的发病机制。

从分子机制来看，在夏科氏足(另一种神经性关节病)中，骨保护素(osteoprotegerin，OPG)、NF-κB受体活化因子(receptor activator of NF-κB，RANK)及NF-κB受体活化因子配体(receptor activator of NF-κB ligand，RANKL)三者所构成的通路会引起严重的骨吸收。骨吸收同样为夏科氏肩关节病的特征之一，故OPG/RANKL/RANK信号通路可能作为外推机制，为夏科氏肩关节病中可能存在的分子发病机制的研究提供参考。

Chiari Ⅰ畸形继发SM致夏科氏肩关节病的发病机制

Chiari Ⅰ畸形(患病率为3/10万~8/10万)主要特征为小脑扁桃体下疝，患者常伴头痛、肢体麻木及四肢轻瘫等症状[8-10]。小脑扁桃体下疝阻塞第四脑室出口，导致脑脊液循环受阻，异常压力传导至脊髓中央管，使65%~85%的患者在颈段或颈胸段(最常为C5~T1节段)形成纵行液腔，即SM[11-13]。空洞扩张破坏了脊髓前角运动神经元及前角间束内的交叉温痛觉纤维，导致患者出现上肢肌力减退及典型的分离性感觉障碍。20%~30%的SM患者会发展为夏科氏肩关节病[4, 6, 11, 14]。其主要机制为：肩关节失去感觉后，患者无法及时察觉日常活动中的反复创伤，如脱位、半脱位、骨折等[4]。由此进入失去神经保护的恶性循环，炎症激活、骨吸收增强、碎片形成、异常重建，最终导致关节破坏、肿胀、畸形(图1)。

Chiari I畸形继发脊髓空洞症在夏科氏肩关节病中的发病机制

title: Phishing detection on webpages in European non-English languages based on machine learning
creator: Dan Komosny
description: Machine learning-based phishing detection is crucial for preventing zero-day attacks. State-of-the-art phishing detection performs well on English webpages. However, it is not adequately accurate for webpages in minor languages. This work significantly improves phishing detection in European countries where minor languages are predominantly spoken.

title: 双相障碍与吸烟导致的脑区活动动态性改变
creator: 茂兴 钟, 淼 张, 斐文 王, 一举 王, 哲宁 刘, 洁 阳
description: 目的双相障碍(bipolar disorder，BD)患者吸烟率较高，吸烟状态可能协同疾病相关脑功能异常，共同影响静息态脑活动。为探究BD诊断与吸烟状态对脑区动态活动不稳定性的独立及交互效应，本研究基于静息态功能磁共振成像(functional magnetic resonance imaging，fMRI)数据，综合动态低频振幅(dynamic amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation，dALFF)、动态分数低频振幅(dynamic fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation，dfALFF)、动态局部一致性(dynamic regional homogeneity，dReHo)评估局部脑活动动态波动，并分析异常脑区与临床症状及每日吸烟量的关系。方法纳入2022年7月至2025年11月中南大学湘雅二医院招募的113名研究对象，包括25名吸烟的BD患者(BDsm组)、33名不吸烟的BD患者(BDnsm组)、23名吸烟的健康对照者(HCsm组)及32名不吸烟的健康对照者(HCnsm组)。BDsm组和BDnsm组合并为BD组，HCsm组和HCnsm组合并为HC组。采集静息态fMRI数据并完成预处理后，采用滑动窗口方法计算dALFF、dfALFF和dReHo。3项动态指标经标准化后进行主成分分析，提取第一主成分作为综合动态脑区活动指标。构建全脑双因素协方差分析模型，分析BD诊断与吸烟状态的主效应及其交互效应，协变量包括年龄、性别、受教育年限和数据集来源；对显著脑区进一步行事后比较及Pearson相关分析。结果全脑分析显示，BD诊断与吸烟状态在右侧丘脑存在显著交互效应。事后分析显示，BDsm组的右侧丘脑动态活动不稳定性显著高于HCsm组( t=3.955， P<0.001)和BDnsm组( t=5.987， P<0.001)，BDnsm组的右侧丘脑动态活动不稳定性低于HCnsm组( t=-6.681， P<0.001)，HCsm组低于HCnsm组( t=-4.530， P<0.001)。控制数据集来源后，该交互效应仍显著，且仅在男性样本中重复分析时结果一致。BD诊断主效应出现在腹内侧前额叶皮层和左侧背外侧前额叶皮层。事后分析显示，BDsm的腹内侧前额叶皮层和左侧背外侧前额叶皮层的动态活动不稳定性均显著高于HCsm组(腹内侧前额叶皮层： t=5.046， P<0.001；左侧背外侧前额叶皮层： t=3.152， P=0.003)，BDnsm的腹内侧前额叶皮层和左侧背外侧前额叶皮层的动态活动不稳定性亦均显著高于HCnsm组(腹内侧前额叶皮层： t=3.440， P=0.001；左侧背外侧前额叶皮层： t=4.684， P<0.001)。未观察到吸烟状态的主效应。全部吸烟者中，每日吸烟量与右侧丘脑动态活动不稳定性呈正相关( r=0.335， P=0.026)；吸烟BD患者左侧背外侧前额叶皮层动态活动不稳定性与焦虑症状呈正相关( r=0.451， P=0.031)。结论BD诊断与吸烟状态对右侧丘脑动态活动存在交互影响。非吸烟状态下，BD患者表现为丘脑动态活动不稳定性降低；在吸烟状态下，BD相关丘脑动态活动降低的表现减弱，并与吸烟暴露强度存在一定关联。BD患者前额叶脑区动态活动不稳定性升高，提示情绪调节和认知控制相关脑区存在动态活动异常。 双相障碍(bipolar disorder，BD)与吸烟之间的关系一直备受关注。根据最新的世界精神卫生调查数据 [ 1]，BD的终身患病率男性为2.5%，女性为2.

title: 脊髓Lamb1参与ACC-SDH通路调控负性情绪易化神经病理性疼痛的机制
creator: 健 王, 卓峰 丁, 伟 徐, 望远 邹, 曲练 郭, 宗斌 宋
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的神经病理性疼痛常伴焦虑、抑郁情绪，形成疼痛-负性情绪共病状态，其具体机制目前仍未阐明。本研究旨在探讨前扣带回皮质(anterior cingulate cortex，ACC)-脊髓背角(spinal dorsal horn，SDH)下行通路在负性情绪易化神经病理性疼痛中的调控机制，筛选并验证其在脊髓水平发挥作用的关键分子。方法采用雄性Sprague-Dawley大鼠构建慢性不可预见性轻度应激(chronic unpredictable mild stress，CUMS)联合慢性缩窄性损伤(chronic constriction injury，CCI)模型，用以模拟负性情绪易化神经病理性疼痛状态。其中，CUMS持续21 d，每日随机给予2种不同应激刺激；CCI模型通过结扎左侧坐骨神经建立。采用糖水偏好实验(sucrose preference test，SPT)和强迫游泳实验评估抑郁样行为，采用von-Frey法检测机械痛阈值。通过向SDH注射逆行腺相关病毒(adeno-associated virus，AAV)-环化重组酶(cyclization recombination enzyme，Cre)、向ACC区注射CRE依赖型hM4Di病毒，结合氯氮平N-氧化物(clozapine-N-oxide，CNO)连续14 d腹腔注射给药，特异性抑制ACC-SDH投射神经元活性，并进行行为学观察。在CCI术后第7天，取腰膨大脊髓组织进行转录组测序，筛选差异表达基因，结合基因本体论(gene ontology，GO)及通路富集分析明确候选分子的功能特征，并采用蛋白质印迹法(Western blotting，WB)和免疫荧光验证候选分子层粘连蛋白β1亚基(laminin subunit beta-1，Lamb1)的表达变化、分布特征及细胞定位。进一步向SDH注射AAV敲减Lamb1的表达，观察其对ACC-SDH通路抑制后镇痛效应及情绪相关行为的影响。结果CUMS处理可诱导大鼠出现明显抑郁样行为，并进一步加重CCI所致机械痛敏。抑制ACC-SDH通路后，自CCI术后第3天至第10天，大鼠的机械痛阈值明显升高，并且在CCI术后第7天最为显著(均P<0.05)。RNA测序结果显示，抑制ACC-SDH神经元活性后脊髓中共有126个差异表达基因，其中94个上调、32个下调，主要涉及细胞外基质、突触功能、神经元结构及疼痛相关过程。Lamb1为上调最显著的候选分子。WB结果证实，特异性抑制ACC-SDH投射神经元活性后，脊髓中Lamb1蛋白的表达水平升高，而CUMS+CCI组脊髓Lamb1表达低于CCI+control组(均P<0.05)。免疫荧光染色结果显示，Lamb1在脊髓中广泛分布，主要富集于SDH浅层，并与神经元、小胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞呈现空间邻近分布。敲减脊髓Lamb1后，可以下调AAV-hM4Di组大鼠的机械痛阈值，并加重CCI大鼠的痛觉过敏。结论Lamb1在脊髓水平参与ACC-SDH通路调控负性情绪易化神经病理性疼痛的过程。本研究从脑-脊髓下行调控角度揭示了疼痛-负性情绪共病的脊髓分子基础，为干预负性情绪相关神经病理性疼痛提供了新策略。 神经病理性疼痛是常见的慢性疼痛，其发病率可达5%~10%[1]。神经病理性疼痛常伴发焦虑、抑郁等负性情绪；而长期存在的负性情绪又可进一步加重患者的疼痛感知，随着病程进展逐渐形成疼痛-负性情绪共病状态，导致神经病理性疼痛迁延难愈，并带来一系列心理、行为及社会问题[2-3]。因此，探究负性情绪与疼痛感知之间的调控机制，对于完善对神经病理性疼痛发病机制的认识及寻找潜在治疗靶点具有重要意义。 前扣带回皮质(anterior cingulate cortex，ACC)是中枢神经系统疼痛相关皮质网络的重要组成部分，不仅参与疼痛情感成分的形成和痛觉调控，也与焦虑、抑郁等负性情绪的发生、发展密切相关[4]。近年来研究[5]发现，脑下行调控系统可通过改变脊髓神经元兴奋性和局部敏化水平参与疼痛的发生、发展。ACC可直接发出投射纤维至脊髓背角(spinal dorsal horn，SDH)，形成ACC-SDH通路，并在疼痛易化中发挥作用[6]。本课题组前期研究[7]发现，在抑郁合并神经病理性疼痛的模型大鼠中，ACC-SDH投射神经元活性增强；抑制ACC-SDH通路活性可缓解负性情绪对神经病理性疼痛的易化作用。然而，该通路在脊髓水平通过何种关键分子介导上述效应，目前尚不清楚。 层粘连蛋白(laminin)是细胞外基质(extracellular matrix，ECM)的重要组成成分，属于由α、β和γ链组成的异源三聚体糖蛋白家族。Laminin β1亚基(laminin subunit beta-1，Lamb1)在皮层中高表达，并参与精神障碍及疼痛-抑郁共病的发生[8-9]。然而，Lamb1在负性情绪易化神经病理性疼痛中的作用，尤其是其是否参与ACC-SDH通路介导的脊髓调控机制，仍缺乏直接证据。 本研究采用慢性不可预见性轻度应激(chronic unpredictable mild stress，CUMS)联合慢性缩窄性损伤(chronic constriction injury，CCI)建立负性情绪易化神经病理性疼痛大鼠模型，并结合化学遗传学、转录组测序、蛋白质印迹法(Western blotting，WB)及免疫荧光等方法，筛选并验证ACC-SDH通路在负性情绪易化神经病理性疼痛过程中所涉及的脊髓关键分子，重点探讨Lamb1在其中的作用，以期为疼痛-负性情绪共病机制研究及潜在干预靶点的筛选提供理论依据。 材料与方法 伦理声明 本研究已通过中南大学湘雅医院医学伦理委员会批准(审批号：2023111570)，所有实验设计与操作均遵循国际疼痛学会的动物实验伦理准则。 实验动物及分组 体重160~180 g的雄性Sprague-Dawley大鼠购自湖南斯莱克景达实验动物有限公司，以4~5只/笼饲养，处于12 h光/暗交替周期，自由摄食、饮水。动物饲养与使用遵循美国国立卫生研究院《实验动物护理和使用指南》。所有动物行为学实验均在双盲条件下进行。CUMS实验中，假手术(Sham)+对照(control)组、Sham+CUMS组、CCI+control组、CCI+CUMS组各6只大鼠。腺相关病毒(adeno-associated virus，AAV)注射实验中，AAV-control组、AAV-化学遗传学抑制(记为hM4Di)组各13只大鼠，其中6只用于行为学检测和c-Fos表达水平验证，3只用于RNA测序、4只用于Lamb1的WB分析；AAV-hM4Di+乱序对照序列(记为scramble)组、AAV-hM4Di+敲减Lamb1(记为siLamb1)组各10只大鼠，其中6只用于行为学检测，4只用于Lamb1的WB分析；CUMS+CCI+scramble组、CUMS+CCI+siLamb1组、CCI+scramble组、CCI+siLamb1组各6只大鼠。 方法 CUMS模型建立 按既往研究[10]中的方法建立CUMS模型，包括食物或饮水剥夺、潮湿或干燥垫料、拥挤或单笼饲养、昼夜节律颠倒、冷水或热水强迫游泳、尾夹、笼具震荡、束缚、噪音及气味刺激等多种应激源。于21 d内每日随机给予2种不同刺激，以保证刺激的不可预见性。 CCI模型建立 采用异氟烷对大鼠进行全身麻醉后，建立神经病理性疼痛CCI模型[11]。钝性分离股二头肌后暴露左侧坐骨神经，采用4-0丝线于坐骨神经周围打4个松结，结间距1 mm。假手术组仅暴露坐骨神经，不进行结扎。对于CUMS+CCI组，大鼠自手术前21 d(记为第-21 d)开始接受CUMS刺激，于手术当天(记为第0天)进行CCI手术。 机械痛阈值测定 大鼠机械痛阈值的测定方法参考既往文献[12]，将大鼠置于测试笼内适应30 min后，使用von-Frey针垂直刺激其左侧足底中部，针丝弯曲并保持2~3 s后，若出现抬足或舔足反应，则记为阳性。每次测量间隔5 min，记录出现阳性反应时的最小刺激强度作为机械痛阈值。 糖水偏好实验 糖水偏好实验(sucrose preference test，SPT)参照既往研究[13]进行。大鼠先适应性饮用1%蔗糖溶液48 h。正式实验前禁水14 h，测试时单笼饲养，每笼放置1瓶1%蔗糖溶液和1瓶纯净水，自由饮用4 h，每2 h交换2个溶液瓶的位置。记录2种液体的摄入量，按蔗糖溶液摄入量除以总液体摄入量计算蔗糖偏好率。 强迫游泳实验 在强迫游泳实验中，将大鼠置于装有水的透明玻璃圆柱体中(直径20 cm，水深30 cm，室温)，方法参照既往研究[14]。前2 min为训练阶段，随后4 min为测试阶段。根据录像，当大鼠停止挣扎、呈漂浮状态时，视为不动，并记录不动时间。计算4 min测试阶段内的总不动时间。 转录组测序 转录组测序由数谱(上海)生物科技有限公司完成。具体实验流程：提取的总RNA样品经琼脂糖电泳和Nanodrop质检和定量后，用寡聚(dT)磁珠富集信使RNA(messenger title: Cervicothoracic Tuberculous Spondylitis in a Toddler: A Case Report
creator: Paul van Schie, Bregje Jaeger, Martijn van der Kuip, Agnita Stadhouder, Ricardo E. Feller
description: Background and Importance Tuberculous spondylitis (or Pott’s disease) is a common form of skeletal tuberculosis. Although primarily treated with tuberculostatic drugs, spinal surgery is necessary in patients with deformities or spinal cord compression. Literature describing surgery strategies in very young children remains scarce. Clinical Presentation A 20-month-old girl presented with torticollis without neurological deficits.

title: The interplay of olfaction and vision in host plant selection by Anthrenus verbasci
creator: Ferenc Deutsch, Sándor Kecskeméti
description: Anthrenus verbasci is commonly associated with museums, where the larvae can destroy valuable collections and displays. In households they are a nuisance; carpets, fabrics, food-items, or any proteinaceous material can be damaged. Little is known about the host preference of adults, they are frequently seen on plants of the Apiaceae, yet we do not know why they are preferred.

title: Distinguishing acute and chronic TMD in adolescent patients
creator: Yeon-Hee Lee, Q-Schick Auh, Seonggwang Jeon, Seong-Woo Jang, Tae-Seok Kim
description: This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to elucidate the clinical and imaging characteristics of chronic temporomandibular disorder (TMD) compared to acute TMD in adolescents, and to identify factors associated with symptom chronicity. The study included 158 adolescent patients with TMD (103 females and 55 males; mean age, 15.08 ± 2.

title: Single-subject detection of speech network activation using functional near-infrared spectroscopy
creator: Carlotta Koch, Androu Abdalmalak, Joan Orpella, Jacob Rottenberg, Eric S. Jackson
description: .SignificanceMost neuroimaging studies rely on group-level analyses, yet many clinical and translational applications require reliable inference at the level of individual participants.AimWe evaluated whether functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) can detect expected speech network related activation patterns at the single-subject level.ApproachTwenty-seven adults completed simple listening and speaking tasks while fNIRS data were recorded over bilateral frontal, temporal, and parietal regions.

title: m7G-related gene signatures determine prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer
creator: Yunxiang Li, Xin Lan, Jianqiao Dong, Jing Li, Bin Wang, Yanhong Wang, Hongyan Jia
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), which lacks targeted treatment options, continues to pose a major clinical hurdle. This study investigated the molecular complexities of TNBC, with a focus on m7G modifications, the immune microenvironment, and their influence on patient prognosis. An integrated analysis of m7G-related genes facilitated the creation of a risk model based on differentially expressed m7G-related genes, which effectively stratified patients with TNBC into low- and high-risk groups, with the low-risk group demonstrating a marked survival advantage.

title: Driving Naive State Induction Using Human Wharton Jelly-Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Conditioned Medium in Rhesus Monkey Embryonic Stem Cells
creator: Preeyanan Anwised, Ratree Moorawong, Worawalan Samruan, Jittanun Srisutush, Sirilak Somredngan, Irene Aksoy, Pierre Savatier, Rangsun Parnpai
description: Highlights What are the main findings? hWJ-MSCs promote primed-to-naive conversion in RhESCs.hWJ-MSCs-CM more robustly induced the expression of key naive markers, including KLF4, KLF17, ESRRB, TFAP2C and DPPA2. What is the implication of the main finding? hWJ-MSCs-CM as a novel culture medium for enhancing naive pluripotency in primate ESCs.hWJ-MSCs provide a human-compatible, xeno-free alternative to traditional MEFs-based systems.

title: Lateral extra‐articular procedures in primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction reduce graft failure rates in elite and competitive athletes: A systematic review
creator: Laurin Kratochwil, Simon Kienberger, Adrian Deichsel, Tobias Gotterbarm, Philipp W Winkler
description: PurposeThe aim of this systematic review was to evaluate clinical outcomes of combined primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and lateral extra‐articular procedures (LEAP) in elite and competitive athletes. Where enough data were available, the review also aimed to differentiate between various LEAP techniques.

title: Prediction of adverse left ventricular remodeling by culprit lesion features in patients with LAD-related myocardial infarction
creator: Jiali Wang, Xuelu Wang, Wenhua Di, Yankai Meng, Tao Ding, Yuan Lu, Chunfeng Hu, Xueyong Wang
description: High-quality evidence regarding the associations between culprit lesion features and cardiac function after post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in ST-segment elevation acute myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients is still needed. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) can be used to visually and quantitatively evaluate myocardial damage.

title: The Incidence of Bone Cement Implantation Syndrome Grade 3 in Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Multicenter Case Series
creator: Karen E. Brokke, Sjoerd Servaas, Inger N. Sierevelt, Karel W.J. Klop, Sef J.A. van Bilsen, Laurens Kaas, Loes W.A.H. van Beers, Erik H.P.A. van Dongen, Rutger van Geenen, W. Anton Visser, Iris Koenraadt-van Oost, Monique A.H. Steegers, Peter A. Nolte
description: Background:Cardiac arrest during hip or knee arthroplasty (KA) represents the most severe manifestation of bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). However, true incidence rates remain uncertain, and data on clinical characteristics and outcomes are limited. The aim of this study was to determine the incidence of BCIS grade 3 in hip and KA and to describe associated clinical characteristics and mortality.

title: Study on urban passenger transport carbon reduction pathways based on system dynamics
creator: Ranqi Liu, Ning Liu
description: Passenger transport carbon emission control is recognized as a critical component in achieving the dual-carbon goals amid accelerating urbanization. A system dynamics model incorporating population and economic factors, energy consumption, traffic operation, and carbon emission control has been developed. Through boundary identification and validation of variable relationships, a simulation model has been established.

title: Reading the Writing on the Wall
creator: Austin M. Beason, Nicole K. Roberts, Youssef El Bitar, Margaret L. Boehler, Cathy J. Schwind, D. Gordon Allan
description: Background:Identifying orthopaedic surgery residents at risk of future professional or practice-related difficulties remains challenging. While knowledge-based assessments such as the Orthopaedic In-Training Examination (OITE) are widely used, they incompletely capture behavioral and professionalism concerns that often underlie significant problems during residency and subsequent practice.

title: Novel AAV843 Vector-Mediated Gene Replacement Therapy Rescues Primary Hyperoxaluria Type I in Mice
creator: Jingjia Zhang, Ye Yin, Baowei Ji, Manqing Sun, Yuanyan Jiang, Xiaohui Wu, Xiao Xiao, Qian Shen, Xia Wu, Hong Xu
description: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder resulting from mutations in the alanine–glyoxylate aminotransferase (AGXT) gene, leading to excessive systemic deposition of calcium oxalate. This condition is an important cause of end-stage renal disease in children and poses a serious threat to patient survival.

title: Molecular and agronomic assessment of faba bean genotypes identifies resistance to Orobanche crenata infestation
creator: Yu Wang, Yossry E Salama, Khaled E Amer, Waly F Elsayed, Salwa A Orabi, Ahmed H El-Sappah, Ehab M B Mahdy, Ehab M Zayed, Mohamed M A Elashtokhy
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Faba bean (Vicia faba L.)(V. faba), an essential legume in Egypt, is severely impacted by broomrape (Orobanche crenata) (O. crenata), a parasitic weed that feeds on roots, making chemical control difficult without harming the crop. Three faba bean genotypes (Giza-843, Misr-3, and Sakha-3) along with nine pure lines were evaluated for resistance to broomrape in field trials (2021–2023) using gene barcoding (rbcL, rpoC1), ten Start Codon Targeted (SCoT) markers, and phonological and agronomic traits to identify resistance sources.

title: A scalable workflow using digital cognitive assessment and pTau217 for MCI detection
creator: Srinivasan Vairavan, Nicholas Griffin, David Wilson, Gallen Triana‐Baltzer, Victoria Brugada‐Ramentol, Elena Vera‐Campuzano, Daniel Alcolea, Silvia Fallone, Lucy Mackintosh, Lindsey Mette, James D Doecke, Joanne Robertson, Larry Ward, Gonzalo Sánchez Benavides, Carolina Minguillon, Clàudia Porta Mas
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). INTRODUCTIONBlood biomarkers like phosphorylated tau (p‐tau)217 offer high diagnostic accuracy for Alzheimer's disease (AD) but face implementation challenges in low‐prevalence settings. We evaluated the Altoida NeuroMarker Platform as a digital cognitive triage tool before plasma p‐tau217 testing.METHODSXGBoost models were trained to predict mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and p‐tau217 status in 688 individuals across Australia, Spain, and the United States using the Altoida NeuroMarker. p‐tau217 status was dichotomized using a threshold of 0.04 pg/mL (LucentAD).

title: Situating emotion regulation in autism and ADHD through neurodivergent adolescents’ perspectives
creator: Georgia Pavlopoulou, Susie Chandler, Steve Lukito, Myrofora Kakoulidou, Maciej Matejko, Isabel Jackson, Beta Balwani, Tiegan Boyens, Dorian Poulton, Luke Harvey-Nguyen, Zoë Glen, Archie Wilson, Elisa Ly, Elizabeth Macauley, Jane Hurry, Sylvan Baker, Edmund J. S. Sonuga-Barke, Georgia Pavlopoulou, Ge
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Accounts of emotional dysregulation in autism and ADHD are typically based on external adult observations anchored in neurotypical notions of appropriate emotional responses1. These often fail to account for neurodivergent people’s efforts to regulate in the context of the upsetting experiences they face, and to explore how neurodivergent young people manage emotional burden or find effective strategies to reduce distress and increase resilience.

title: Mechanistic and Life-Cycle Framework for Green Nanomaterials in Atmospheric Water Harvesting
creator: Noor Al-Sadeq, Johar Amin Ahmed Abdullah, Alberto Romero, Víctor M. Perez-Puyana
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) has been recognized as a promising technology to address global freshwater scarcity in a decentralized manner. Nevertheless, conventional AWH sorbents are often associated with high energy consumption, toxic synthesis procedures, and short operational lifetimes. To address such limitations, a comprehensive review paper develops a unified framework to bridge the gap between nanoscale material properties, such as synthesis routes, structural architecture, and adsorption thermodynamics, and macro-scale environmental and economic performance.

title: Real-world outcomes of faricimab in treatment-naïve diabetic macular edema: The Middle East perspective

description: PURPOSE:Diabetic macular edema (DME) is a major cause of visual impairment in patients with diabetic retinopathy. While intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) monotherapy has been considered standard of care, many patients have suboptimal treatment responses. Faricimab, which targets angiopoietin-2 and VEGF-A, has shown efficacy and tolerability in randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

title: Experimental evidence for social learning in semi-natural, wild-type Norway rats
creator: Sacha C. Engelhardt, Harshkumar Vasoya, Michael Taborsky
description: Animals may acquire information about their environment by social learning. Social transmission can affect the rate of trait acquisition and performance. It is often unclear, how behaviours are acquired when social information is available. In particular, the role of social learning in the acquisition of non-intuitive tasks is currently obscure.

title: Microalgae and Cyanobacteria in the Obesity Evidence Landscape: A PRISMA-ScR Scoping Review with Mechanistic and Safety Mapping
creator: Quoc-Phong Huynh, Quoc-Dang Quan, Viet-The Ho, Quang-Tri Le, Huu-Cuong Nguyen, Hoang-Dung Tran
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryMicroalgae and cyanobacteria contain a wide range of bioactive compounds that have been explored in obesity-related research, but the literature is dispersed across study types and often reported in ways that are hard to compare. We assembled and mapped the accessible full-text evidence to show where research density is highest, where mechanistic reporting is thin, and how often safety considerations are documented.

title: Upscaling effects on infectious disease emergence risk emphasize the need for local planning in primary prevention within biodiversity hotspots
creator: Renata L. Muylaert, David A. Wilkinson, Evita Izza Dwiyanti, David T. S. Hayman
description: Zoonotic risk assessments are increasingly vital in the wake of recent epidemics. The microbial diversity of parasitic organisms correlates with host species richness, with regions of high biodiversity facing elevated risks of emerging zoonotic infections. While habitat loss and fragmentation reduce species diversity, anthropogenic encroachment, particularly in forested areas, amplifies human exposure to novel pathogens.

title: Individualized cholinergic pathway degeneration in Alzheimer's disease characterized by normative modeling

These models were applied to 1742 scans from 725 participants in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort.
