title: Management of Geriatric Ankle Fractures
creator: Lyndon Mason, Chijioke Orji, Jan Szatkowski
description: Purpose of ReviewThis review evaluates current management options for managing ankle fractures in geriatric patients with osteoporosis. It addresses the challenges posed by compromised bone integrity and examines operative and non-operative approaches to promote early mobility and functional recovery in elderly individuals.Recent FindingsRecent studies show that both surgical and non-surgical management can yield comparable functional outcomes, but complication profiles differ.

title: Recurrent abdominal pain as a leading symptom for branchio-oto-renal syndrome: a case report
creator: Alaa Senjab, Omar Al Ayoubi, Grace Tannous, Yaman Alsharef
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBranchio-oto-renal syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by hearing impairment, branchial arch anomalies, preauricular pits, and renal malformations. Although recurrent abdominal pain is not a classic feature, it can arise owing to renal complications such as hydronephrosis.Case presentationAn 8-year-old Arab boy with a history of congenital sensorineural hearing loss presented to the emergency department with recurrent right flank pain radiating to the anterior abdomen occurring approximately every 2 weeks over 4 months.

title: SLIRP differentially modulates RNA binding of pathogenic LRPPRC variants
creator: Louise Lambert, Urška Rovšnik, Amandine Moretton, Katarina Johansson, Mãdãlina Sãcultanu, Mathilde Chéron, Adèle Porcan, Bertil Macao, Siet van den Wildenberg, Xuefeng Zhu, Maria Falkenberg, Géraldine Farge
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The LRPPRC/SLIRP complex is a key post-transcriptional regulator of mitochondrial gene expression, stabilizing mitochondrial mRNAs and promoting their polyadenylation and translation. Mutations in LRPPRC cause mitochondrial disorders, including Leigh syndrome French-Canadian type (LSFC), primarily affecting oxidative phosphorylation. Here, we examined the RNA-binding properties of wild-type LRPPRC and three pathogenic variants (A354V, K909del, and R1276_K1300del) using electrophoretic mobility shift assays, acoustic force spectroscopy, and AlphaFold 3 modeling.

title: K-operator for Modelling Neurodegeneration: Simulations, fMRI Application, Eigenvalue Analysis and Recurrence Plots
creator: Sofia Fazio, Patrizia Ribino, Francesca Gasparini, Norbert Marwan, Peppino Fazio, Marco Gherardi, Maria Mannone
description: The brain network damage provoked by a neurological disease can be modelled as the result of the action of an operator, K, acting on the brain, inspired by physics. Here, we explore the matrix formulation of K, analysing eigenvalues and eigenvectors, with heuristic considerations on different techniques to approximate it.

title: Distinct diurnal temperature rhythm patterns in critical illness myopathy: secondary analysis of two prospective trials
creator: D. Mewes, S. Weber-Carstens, K. Rubarth, S. D. Boie, C. Spies, A. Kramer, J. Fielitz, T. Wollersheim, B. Ananthasubramaniam, F. Braune, L. Hancke, L. Spies, F. Balzer, L. J. Engelhardt
description: BackgroundCritical illness myopathy (CIM) increases mortality and causes long-term disabilities. CIM is characterized by reduced muscle excitability, muscle atrophy, weakness, and impaired glucose metabolism. Functional circadian rhythms are important for skeletal muscle homeostasis. Circadian rhythms are often disrupted during critical illness in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

title: 二甲双胍调控AKT/mTOR通路抑制前列腺癌的机制
creator: Zhengkun Zhang, Zhiyou Quan, Panpan Dai, Keyi Xu, Zhaoru Yin, Dan Chen, Ruiman Geng, Xuxu Ji, Dingxue Wang, Shu Chen, Lihong Chen, Ji Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的 探讨二甲双胍对前列腺癌细胞增殖、迁移和侵袭的影响，并分析其是否通过调控人类抗原R（human antigen R, HuR）及AKT/mTOR信号通路发挥抗肿瘤作用。方法 取人前列腺癌细胞PC3和22RV1细胞系，采用二甲双胍干预，并结合HuR敲低和过表达实验进一步验证其作用机制。采用细胞计数试剂盒-8（cell counting kit-8, CCK-8）检测细胞增殖活性，Transwell实验检测细胞迁移和侵袭能力，实时荧光定量PCR（quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction, qRT-PCR）和Western blot检测HuR及AKT/mTOR信号通路相关蛋白的表达水平。结果 二甲双胍干预可降低PC3和22RV1细胞的增殖、迁移和侵袭能力，并抑制AKT/mTOR通路相关蛋白的表达（P<0.05）。敲低HuR后，前列腺癌细胞的增殖、迁移和侵袭能力同样下降，AKT/mTOR通路活性受到抑制。相反，过表达HuR可部分减弱二甲双胍对前列腺癌细胞恶性生物学行为及AKT/mTOR通路的抑制作用。此外，二甲双胍可呈浓度依赖性下调PC3和22RV1细胞中HuR的mRNA和蛋白表达水平（P<0.01）。结论 二甲双胍可能通过下调HuR表达，抑制AKT/mTOR信号通路活化，从而降低前列腺癌细胞的增殖、迁移和侵袭能力。Keywords: 前列腺癌, 二甲双胍, 人类抗原R, AKT, mTOR 前列腺癌（prostate cancer, PCa）是男性泌尿生殖系统中最常见的恶性肿瘤。根据GLOBOCAN统计，2022年新增PCa病例1466680例，死亡病例占男性所有癌症死亡病例的4.1%[1]，2022年中国前列腺癌新发病例约13.4万例，死亡病例约4.8万例[2]。因此，PCa逐渐成为威胁中老年男性健康的主要问题。 二甲双胍是治疗2型糖尿病（type 2 diabetes mellitus, T2DM）的一线药物，已经在临床上使用超过50年，具有良好的安全性[3]。2005年，Evans等[4]研究发现T2DM患者在二甲双胍治疗后发生癌症的风险较低。从那时起，越来越多的研究表明二甲双胍可以抑制许多类癌症的发展[5-8]。同时，二甲双胍对亚洲T2DM患者中的PCa具有潜在的保护作用。与其他抗糖尿病药物相比，二甲双胍可以显著降低T2DM患者PCa的风险，改善预后，并延缓PCa的进展[9-10]。先前的研究表明，二甲双胍通过激活AMPK、抑制mTOR信号传导和蛋白质合成以及阻断细胞周期进展作为抗癌剂[11-12]。 RNA结合蛋白（RNA bingding protein, RBP）可通过与mRNA的特异性结合直接或间接调节mRNA的功能，例如介导mRNA运输、定位和翻译[13-14]。HuR是一种常见的RNA 结合蛋白，通过与富含腺嘌呤-尿嘧啶元件结合来调节mRNA的稳定性和转录。HuR在包括PCa在内的几种癌症中过表达[15]。此外，HuR表达的上调与肿瘤侵袭和不良预后有关[16]，也可以促进肿瘤细胞的增殖、迁移和血管生成[17-18]。 在此研究中，我们验证二甲双胍对PCa细胞活性的影响，通过生物信息学分析、体外实验探索HuR在二甲双胍调控PCa细胞中的关键作用。 材料与方法 细胞培养和转染 质粒（siHuR）及其阴性对照siRNA（siNC）购自中国RiboBio公司，过表达HuR质粒（pHuR）及其阴性对照质粒（pNC）购自中国GenePharma公司。使用美国Invitrogen公司Lipofectamine 2000TM转染细胞24 h。 CCK8细胞毒性测定 title: 身体扫描正念训练在灼口综合征患者中应用效果评价
creator: Jing He, Ning Xiao, Mingjia Hu, Jia Li, Fan Liu
description: 目的通过应用身体扫描正念训练对灼口综合征（Burning mouth syndrome, BMS）患者进行干预，评价其临床应用效果。方法本研究采用随机、对照、盲法评估的临床研究设计方案，利用随机数字表法将通过纳入排除标准筛选的BMS患者分为对照组和试验组。对照组采用药物治疗及常规心理护理措施，试验组在对照组基础上增加2周身体扫描正念训练。在干预前、干预后及干预后3个月采用视觉模拟评分法（Visual Analogue Scale, VAS）、失眠严重指数量表（Insomnia Severity Index, ISI）、广泛性焦虑量表（Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, GAD-7）、患者健康问卷抑郁量表（Patient Health Questionnaire-9, PHQ-9）及口腔健康影响程度量表（Oral Health Impact Profile-14, OHIP-14）分别评估患者的疼痛程度、睡眠质量、焦虑程度、抑郁程度及口腔健康相关生活质量。通过比较两组干预前后主要结局指标（VAS）及次要结局指标（ISI、GAD-7、PHQ-9及OHIP-14）的变化差异，评估身体扫描正念训练对BMS患者的干预效果。结果本研究共纳入80例研究对象，失访3例，最终77例（对照组38例，试验组39例）患者纳入分析。干预后试验组VAS、 ISI、GAD-7及PHQ-9减少的差值中位数（P25,P75）分别为2.00 (1.00, 3.00)、3.00 (0.00, 8.00)、3.00 (1.00, 6.75)和 2.00 (0.00, 5.00)，均大于对照组减少的差值〔0.95 (0.00, 2.50)、0.00 (0.00, 3.00) 、1.00 (0.00, 3.25)和1.00 (0.00, 2.00) 〕，差异有统计学意义（P < 0.05）；两组OHIP-14减少的差值差异无统计学意义（P > 0.05）。干预后及干预后3个月试验组VAS均低于对照组，差异有统计学意义（P < 0.05）。结论BMS患者在常规药物治疗的基础上进行身体扫描正念训练，能有效缓解其口腔烧灼样疼痛程度，也有助于改善睡眠质量、缓解焦虑及抑郁情绪，值得在临床中推广应用。Keywords: 灼口综合征, 身体扫描, 正念, 疼痛 灼口综合征（burning mouth syndrome, BMS）是临床最常见的口腔黏膜病之一，是以口腔黏膜烧灼样疼痛为主要临床表现的一组症候群，但患者口内无明显的临床损害体征[1]。据报道，普通人群中BMS的患病率为1.73%，临床患者中为7.

title: Integrating frailty and cumulative lipid burden for stroke risk stratification: a machine learning–guided Athero-Frailty Score from the CHARLS cohort

description: BackgroundTraditional lipid indices, such as the cumulative Atherogenic Index of Plasma (cumAIP), demonstrate inconsistent predictive performance for stroke in older adults, likely due to the modifying effects of complex medication regimens. title: Entrectinib binds to HMGB1 and activates cardiomyocyte autophagy by inhibiting OTUD5-MTORC1 signaling to induce cardiotoxicity

title: 植入式静脉输液港患者导管阻塞风险预测模型的构建与验证
creator: Shuang Zhang, Suli Han, Ningjun Zhao
description: 目的探讨植入式静脉输液港（implantable venous access port，IVAP）患者发生导管阻塞的影响因素，并构建风险预测模型。方法回顾性选取2022年1月—2024年3月行IVAP置入的563例患者，按7∶3比例随机分为建模组（n=394）与验证组（n=169）。采用单因素分析和多因素logistic回归（双向逐步回归法）筛选导管阻塞的独立影响因素，据此构建列线图预测模型，并分别从区分度、校准度及临床实用性三方面对模型进行验证与评估。结果563例IVAP患者中，导管阻塞发生率为12.79%（72/563）。多因素logistic回归分析显示，体质指数（body mass index，BMI）≥24 kg/m2（OR=3.535，95%CI：1.500～8.329）、合并糖尿病（OR=3.723，95%CI：1.540～8.999）、合并恶性肿瘤（OR=3.161，95%CI：1.327～7.526）、血栓史（OR=3.324，95%CI：1.425～7.755）、D-二聚体升高（OR=547.088，95%CI：46.093～649.462）及导管留置时间≥6个月（OR=2.633，95%CI：1.060～6.543）是导管阻塞的独立危险因素，而定期维护（OR=0.200，95%CI：0.080～0.499）为其独立保护因素（均P<0.05）。建模组受试者工作特征（receiver operating characteristic，ROC）曲线下面积（area under the curve，AUC）为0.91（95%CI：0.87～0.96），验证组AUC为0.94（95%CI：0.88～1.00）；Hosmer-Lemeshow检验显示建模组（χ2=10.782，P=0.214）与验证组（χ2=3.744，P=0.879）模型拟合均良好；决策曲线分析（decision curve analysis，DCA）提示模型具有正向净临床收益。结论本研究构建的IVAP导管阻塞风险预测模型具有良好的预测效能与临床实用价值，可为医护人员早期识别高危患者、实施个性化护理干预提供科学依据，有助于降低导管阻塞的发生风险。Keywords: 植入式静脉输液港, 导管阻塞, 危险因素, 预测模型 植入式静脉输液港（implantable venous access port，IVAP）是一种完全植入皮下、可长期留置的闭合式静脉输液装置，广泛应用于肿瘤化疗、长期肠外营养支持等领域[1]。该装置具有留置时间长、管理便捷、美观隐蔽及感染率低等优势，可为患者建立安全、稳定的静脉通路，有效减少反复穿刺所带来的痛苦[2]。随着IVAP临床应用的日益普及，置管后相关并发症的问题也愈加受到关注[3-4]。其中，导管阻塞是IVAP留置期间最常见且较为严重的非感染性并发症，不仅影响治疗药物的按时输注，延误患者病情，还可能导致非计划性拔管，增加患者痛苦及医疗负担[5-6]。导管阻塞的发生机制复杂，既与导管自身结构、置管位置及临床操作规范密切相关，也受患者个体差异、基础疾病类型及治疗方案等多种因素影响[7]。目前，针对导管阻塞的临床处理主要依赖于经验性措施，如导管冲洗、药物溶栓等[8]，但对于复杂病例，单纯依赖经验仍存在一定的局限性。因此，构建IVAP导管阻塞风险预测模型，对早期识别高危患者、实施个体化预防策略具有重要意义。本研究拟分析IVAP导管阻塞的影响因素，构建并验证风险预测模型，为临床决策提供参考。 对象与方法 研究对象 参照logistic回归分析样本量估算方法[9]，样本量需为自变量个数的10倍。本研究拟纳入25个自变量，考虑20%的无效样本，为保证模型稳定性，建模组至少需要样本量300例。最终纳入2022年1月—2024年3月于我院接受IVAP置入的患者563例，按置入时间顺序以7∶3比例分为建模组（n=394）与验证组（n=169）。纳入标准：①年龄≥18岁；②符合IVAP手术适应证[10]；③于我院行IVAP置入手术；④自愿参与研究并签署知情同意书。排除标准：①合并全身感染者；②凝血功能障碍者；③合并严重慢性阻塞性肺疾病者。本研究经徐州医科大学附属医院医学伦理委员会审批通过（XYFY2025-KL242-01)。 ALB）、血小板计数（platelet count, PLT）、凝血酶原时间（prothrombin time, PT）、活化部分凝血活酶时间（activated partial thromboplastin time, APTT）、凝血酶时间（thrombin time, TT）、纤维蛋白原（fibrinogen, Fib）、D-二聚体；④ IVAP相关信息：首次穿刺是否失败、操作时间、植入部位、导管留置时间、导管材质、定期维护等。 统计学方法 采用SPSS 27.0与R 4.4.0软件进行数据分析。定性资料以例数（百分比）描述，组间比较采用χ2检验；正态分布的定量资料以描述，组间比较采用独立样本t检验；偏态分布的定量资料以中位数（四分位间距）〔M（Q₁，Q₃）〕描述，组间比较采用非参数检验（Mann-Whitney U检验）。采用多因素logistic回归（双向逐步回归法，α入=0.05，α出=0.

title: Intensity-modulated radiotherapy/Volumetric modulated Arc therapy including four Brachytherapy fractions versus 3D conformal radiotherapy containing five Brachytherapy fractions in the treatment of cervical cancer
creator: Barin Feroz, Christoph Ebner, Sergej Skvortsov, Ricarda Purtscheller, Katharina Steger, Magdalena Steinlechner, Miriam Emmelheinz, Jana Rieker, Katharina Leitner, Ute Ganswindt, Sarah Maier, Christian Marth, Alain Gustave Zeimet
description: BackgroundDefinitive radiochemotherapy with external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy is standard for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). Advanced techniques like intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) and volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) have replaced 3D-conformal radiotherapy (3DCRT). This study compares two institutional definitive radiotherapy treatment pathways implemented in different time periods: 3DCRT with five BT fractions and IMRT/VMAT with four BT fractions.

title: PPARα在UVB诱导皮肤损伤中的作用及潜在机制研究
creator: Fengdi Jiang, Yifan Liu, Mingyu Wang, Xiaotao Xie, Adili Maheliya, Mengjie Du, Jiajia Wang, Hai Xiong, Shuyu Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的太阳光中的中波紫外线（ultraviolet B, UVB）是WHO 1类致癌物，可以被表皮吸收，过量UVB照射会导致皮肤损伤和光老化。过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体α（perixisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha, PPARα）是核受体家族的重要成员，在脂质代谢中发挥核心作用。本研究以PPARα－/－与野生型小鼠为对象，旨在观察并探讨PPARα缺失对UVB照射后损伤进程的影响及皮肤脂质谱的变化。方法采用单次高剂量UVB照射（2 J/cm2）构建小鼠皮肤紫外光损伤模型，将C57BL/6J小鼠分为PPARα－/－组和野生型组，通过皮肤光损伤评分、苏木精-伊红（HE）染色、Western blot进行定性与定量分析。另采用连续多次低剂量UVB照射构建小鼠皮肤紫外光老化模型，将C57BL/6小鼠分为PPARα－/－组和野生型组，同样以HE染色和Western blot进行检测。此外，分别采集接受或不接受单次高剂量UVB照射（2 J/cm2）的两种基因型小鼠皮肤样本进行脂质组学分析。结果在急性光损伤模型中，与野生型组小鼠相比，PPARα－/－组小鼠于照射后第0～32天内皮肤光损伤评分显著升高，伤口愈合速度更慢。在光老化模型中，与野生型组小鼠相比，PPARα－/－组小鼠皮肤细胞中衰老相关蛋白质表达水平上调（p16: 0.11±0.02 vs. 0.82±0.18, P<0.05； p21: 0.54±0.03 vs. 1.29±0.07, P<0.01；p53: 0.54±0.04 vs. 1.33±0.06, P<0.01；β-半乳糖苷酶: 0.80±0.06 vs. 1.20±0.15, P<0.05），同时皮肤毛囊数量减少、形态皱缩。脂质组学分析结果显示，UVB照射下PPARα缺失显著加剧了皮肤脂质代谢的紊乱，涉及神经酰胺（d18:1/30:2）、O-酰基-ω-羟基脂肪酸（44:4）、磷脂酰乙醇胺（50:1）、溶血磷脂酰胆碱（19:1）、溶血磷脂酰丝氨酸（44:11）和磷脂酰胆碱（19:1/20:1）等多种脂质的异常表达。结论PPARα可以减轻UVB诱导的皮肤损伤和光老化，其缺失会加重皮肤损伤和脂质代谢紊乱。Keywords: 紫外线, 光损伤, 光老化, 过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体α, 脂质组学 皮肤不仅是人体最大的器官，更是应对外界环境压力的第一道物理屏障。中波紫外线（ultraviolet B, UVB）是诱发皮肤光损伤和光老化的主要环境因子[1-2]。急性暴露于过量UVB可诱发皮肤红斑、水肿及急性炎症反应[3-4]；而慢性累积性暴露则驱动皮肤结构和功能的显著退行性改变，典型特征包括粗糙皱纹、皮肤松弛、色素沉着异常以及胶原蛋白等细胞外基质的降解，并显著增加皮肤癌和光线性皮肤病的易感性[5-6]。UVB致损的核心分子机制主要涉及直接DNA损伤和触发活性氧（reactive oxygen species, ROS）爆发性生成，进而激活氧化应激和炎症级联反应，从而加速皮肤衰老和病理损伤的进程[7-8]。 UVB不仅会导致皮肤DNA损伤和炎症反应，还会改变皮肤脂质的组成。研究表明，UVB照射会导致大鼠角质形成细胞中磷脂酰胆碱、溶血磷脂酰胆碱、磷脂酰乙醇胺和神经酰胺水平上调，鞘磷脂和磷脂酰丝氨酸含量下调[9]；长期亚红斑剂量UVB照射则会显著减少无毛小鼠角质层中的神经酰胺、游离脂肪酸和胆固醇[10]。因此，脂质代谢紊乱可能是UVB诱导皮肤病理改变的重要环节。过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体α（perixisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha, PPARα）属于核受体超家族成员，也是一种转录因子，它是脂质代谢的关键调控因子，能够通过促进脂肪酸氧化、调控脂质合成与分解来维持细胞和组织的脂质稳态[11-12]。已有研究表明，PPARα缺失会加重电离辐射所致的皮肤损伤[13-14]。由此推测，PPARα可能通过影响脂质代谢途径，从而在一定程度上决定UVB诱导的皮肤损伤和光老化的严重程度。然而，目前关于PPARα在UVB诱导的皮肤损伤和光老化中的作用以及PPARα缺失对UVB照射后皮肤脂质的影响尚未见报道。 基于此，本研究采用C57BL/6背景的PPARα基因敲除小鼠和野生型小鼠，构建单次大剂量UVB诱导的皮肤损伤模型以及多次小剂量UVB诱导的光老化模型，比较两者在皮肤外观改变、组织学结构、衰老相关蛋白质表达以及损伤修复能力等方面的差异。同时，结合液相色谱-串联质谱脂质组学技术，对不同处理条件下的皮肤脂质组成进行全面分析，揭示PPARα在维持皮肤脂质稳态、减轻UVB诱导皮肤损伤及光老化中的关键作用。本研究不仅有助于阐明紫外线导致皮肤损伤的代谢机制，也为开发以脂质代谢和PPARα为靶点的防护及干预策略提供理论依据。 材料与方法 实验动物和试剂 野生型（wild-type, WT）C57BL/6雄性小鼠（6～8周龄，体质量18～20 g）购于成都达硕实验动物公司，PPARα基因敲除(PPARα－/－)C57BL/6雄性小鼠（6～8周龄，体质量18～20 g）购于苏州大学动物研究所。磷酸盐缓冲溶液（phosphate buffer saline, PBS）、SDS-PAGE蛋白质上样缓冲液购于上海碧云天生物；GAPDH、p16、p21、p53、β-galactosidase一抗购于美国Cell Signaling Technology；HRP标记二抗购于英国Abcam；ECL化学发光超敏显色试剂盒购于上海翌圣生物；法国Bio-Sun紫外线辐照仪（UVB波长312 nm）。 PPARα－/－繁育与基因型鉴定 title: 血流限制训练对老年肌少症患者肌力及躯体功能的影响
creator: 玉祥 梁, 玉琦 午, 雪丽 淳, 锐莉 王, 佼佼 蒋
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的探讨血流限制训练对住院老年肌少症患者肌肉力量、躯体功能、功能性移动能力及日常生活活动能力的影响，并比较其与传统抗阻训练的差异，为临床制定康复策略提供科学依据。方法本研究采用随机对照试验设计，共纳入40例经临床诊断为肌少症的住院老年患者，按1∶1比例通过计算机生成随机分配序列分为试验组和对照组，各20例。试验组进行血流限制训练，对照组进行抗阻训练，干预持续12 周，每周3 次。分别于干预前、第4周及第12周对受试者进行评估。主要结局指标为肌肉力量，用优势手握力评估。次要结局指标包括躯体功能、功能性移动能力和日常生活活动能力，分别用简易体能状况量表（short physical performance battery, SPPB）、6 m步速和计时起立－行走测试（timed up and go test, TUG）以及改良的Barthel指数（modified barthel index, MBI）进行测量。结果研究期间无失访，无不良事件发生。干预4周后，两组主要结局指标握力均较基线提升（均P<0.001），试验组握力〔（24.35±5.43） kg〕高于对照组〔（20.96±5.25） kg〕，但两组间差异无统计学意义（P=0.051）；在次要结局指标方面，试验组在SPPB评分和MBI评分方面均明显优于对照组（均P<0.05），TUG测试和6 m步速差异尤为明显（P<0.01）。干预12周后，主要结局指标握力在组间差异上具有统计学意义〔试验组（25.25±5.34） kg，对照组（21.66±5.26） kg，P=0.039〕。在次要结局指标方面，试验组在SPPB评分、6 m步速、TUG测试时间和MBI评分方面均明显优于对照组（均P<0.01）。结论血流限制训练能够明显改善住院老年肌少症患者的肌力、提高老年人躯体功能、功能性移动能力及日常生活活动能力，其效果优于抗阻训练。 肌少症是一种与年龄增长相关的渐进性全身骨骼肌病变，其核心症状包括肌肉量减少、肌力下降及/或躯体功能减退[1]。流行病学研究显示，全球60岁以上老龄人口的肌少症发病率达10%～27%[2]，我国老年人群总患病率为18.4%[3]。在住院老年人群中，由于活动受限及共病等因素，肌少症发生率更高，常导致功能衰退加剧、住院时间延长及医疗负担加重[4-6]。传统抗阻训练虽为主要推荐的运动干预方式，但其高负荷特性对常伴多种疾病、虚弱或耐受性差的住院老年人而言，实施依从性与安全性面临挑战[7-8]。近年来，血流限制训练（blood flow restriction training, BFRT）作为一种抗阻训练替代方案广受关注[9]。它通过在运动肢体近端加压，部分限制血流，使患者在低负荷下运动，即可模拟高强度训练引发的肌肉适应[10-11]。已有研究证实BFRT对健康及社区老年肌少症人群的肌力、肌肉量等功能有改善作用且具备安全性[11-12]。然而，现有研究针对住院老年肌少症患者的研究较少且功能评估多限于肌力与肌肉质量，缺乏对躯体功能与日常活动能力的多维综合评估。因此，本研究旨在通过随机对照试验，探讨BFRT对住院老年肌少症患者躯体功能的影响，综合评估其肌力、步行速度及功能独立性等方面的干预效果。 资料与方法 研究对象 本研究于2024年8月至2025年8月在四川大学华西医院招募老年肌少症住院患者，受试者经过严格筛查并签署知情同意书后入组。纳入标准：（1）符合亚洲肌少症工作组2019年制定的肌少症诊断标准[13-14]；（2）年龄>65岁，自身基础疾病稳定、生命体征平稳；（3）可以日常沟通并能理解与合作。排除标准：（1）存在重度功能障碍（MBI≤40分或依赖轮椅/卧床）；（2）严重认知功能障碍或其他精神疾病；（3）血流限制训练禁忌证：深静脉血栓形成史或潜在危险、凝血功能障碍、静脉曲张等。以主要结局指标握力为依据进行样本量估算：采用 G*Power 3.1 软件，设定双侧 α=0.05、检验效能 80%，预估所需最小样本量为 28 例；考虑到约20%的脱落及不依从风险，最终纳入40例临床诊断为肌少症的老年住院患者。 试验方法 本研究为一项随机对照试验，方案已经四川大学华西医院生物医学伦理委员会批准，批准号2024年审（2579）号，并在ClinicalTrials.gov注册（注册号：NCT06986395）。40例纳入者按 1∶1 比例随机分为试验组和对照组。随机分配序列由计算机生成，对结局评估者、数据采集与统计分析人员实施设盲。两组干预均为每周3次，每次30 min，持续12周，并分别于干预前、第4周和第12周进行评估：主要结局指标为握力，次要结局指标包括简易体能状况量表（short physical performance battery, SPPB）评分、6 米步速、计时起立－行走测试（timed up and go test, TUG）时间及改良 Barthel 指数（modified barthel index, MBI）评分。所有干预及评估措施均由经培训人员规范实施。干预主要在患者住院期间完成，对于在研究周期内部分病情稳定提前出院的患者，提供详细的家庭训练指导与简易设备，并通过每周电话或视频随访确保干预依从性与规范性，所有患者均按计划返院完成各时间点评估。研究流程见图1。 Study flowchart 研究流程图 干预方法 所有患者随机分组后，进行运动安全宣教及常规护理，并间接测量患者上下肢的一次最大重复值（one repetition maximum，1RM）[15]，两组训练过程均由专业、经验丰富的康复治疗师进行一对一指导，试验组接受血流限制训练，对照组进行常规抗阻训练。 血流限制训练干预 该方案以“低负荷血流限制训练”为核心，加压设置如下：上肢训练时加压带置于上臂上1/3处，下肢训练时置于大腿近心端距腹股沟5～10 cm处[16]；初始压力设定参考肢体围度及既往文献（上肢80～100 mmHg、下肢150～200 mmHg，1 mmHg =0.133 kPa），并根据患者主观耐受度（RPE评分12～14分）及皮肤颜色、末梢循环情况进行个体化调整[17]；并于每组动作前充压、组间维持压力，训练结束后立即释放，根据个体耐受度调整以避免不适。训练参数设定为负荷强度20%～30% 1RM，每组10～15次重复，共完成4组，组间休息60 s，每周3次，每次30 min，持续12周[18]。单次训练内容包括肱二头肌屈伸、肩部复合动作（前平举、侧平举）以及股四头肌屈伸膝训练，各项均以坐位姿势双侧执行，每组10～15次。 抗阻训练 该方案以中高强度抗阻训练为核心，训练参数设定为负荷强度65%～75% 1RM，每组10～15次重复，共完成4组，组间休息60 s，每周3次，每次30 min，持续12周。单次训练动作内容与试验组相同，本研究比较的是两种不同训练处方（低负荷BFRT vs 中高强度传统抗阻训练）的整体效果，而非单纯的加压因素。

description: BackgroundRetinol (ROL) is essential in dermatology for antiaging; however, its clinical utility is frequently limited by inherent chemical instability and significant cutaneous irritation.ObjectiveThis study describes the development of bakuchiol ferulate (BF), a novel molecular hybrid synthesized from bakuchiol and a ferulic acid (FA) analog. The study aimed to evaluate BF as a stable, well‐tolerated, and efficacious alternative to ROL.

title: Enigmatic odyssey: A case of Behcet disease with atypical thrombotic complications
creator: Hamza A Abdul-Hafez, Yazan Hamdan, Nizar Ayed Abu Hamdeh, Haitham Abu Khadija, Doha Jaber, Mohammad Alnees
description: Introduction and importanceBehçet disease is a rare, chronic, multi-systemic inflammatory disease of unknown origin that affects vessels in various organs. It is characterized by multiple clinical manifestations, most prominently oral and genital ulcers. Typically diagnosed in individuals aged 20 to 40 years with a male predominance, Behçet disease poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges.

title: Predictors for quality of life improvement in schizophrenia: a prospective study of patients in hospital-based rehabilitation programs
creator: Xue Wang, Xue Yang, Wei Jiang, Dan-na Zhou, Wen Wang, Wen-qing Jin, Yi-lang Tang, Yan-ping Ren, Chun-lin Yang
description: BackgroundEnhancing quality of life (QoL) is a crucial goal in the rehabilitation of patients with schizophrenia (SCZ). Identifying factors associated with the outcomes of rehabilitation is of clinical importance. This study examined predictors of subjective QoL (SQoL) outcomes in SCZ patients undergoing a structured 24-week rehabilitation program.MethodsA total of 235 patients with SCZ completed the program.

title: IFPHOR0094 Integrating the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) Framework to Assess the Impact of Active Travel Reward Incentives on Risk Factors Related to Non-Communicable Diseases: A Rapid Review
creator: Kethakee Andaraweera, Georgina Shadrick, James Wright, Arpana Verma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundNon-communicable diseases (NCDs) are leading global causes of morbidity and mortality, while active travel (walking, cycling and wheeling) reduces risks of obesity, NCDs and related mortality. Incentive programmes targeting behaviour change play an important role in improving healthy behaviours.

title: Assessment of large language model chatbots for hemodialysis meal planning: a descriptive study
creator: Kevin Shi, Hiba Hamdan, Elizabeth Cheng, Delphine S Tuot
description: BackgroundLarge language models (LLMs) have the potential to improve nutritional counseling for patients with end stage kidney disease (ESKD). This study evaluates the utility of publicly available LLMs in generating meal plans for individuals receiving hemodialysis.MethodsFifty hypothetical patient profiles were generated from United States national data and used to prompt four LLM chatbots, ChatGPT-o3-mini ® (OpenAI), Claude Sonnet 3.

title: Sex differences in the prescription of antihypertensive medications in primary care patients: an observational study
creator: Elisa Dal Canto, Sophie L Theunisse, Michiel L Bots, Frans Rutten, Marion Biermans, N Charlotte Onland-Moret, Wilko Spiering, Birsen Kiliç, Hester M den Ruijter, Monika Hollander
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPharmacological prescription guidelines for hypertension lack differentiation between the sexes, despite reported sex differences in prevalence, awareness, pathophysiology, and pharmacological response.AimTo assess prescription patterns of blood pressure-lowering medication among females and males in primary care.Design & settingIn this observational study, which was undertaken in the Netherlands, we analysed data collected in 2018 during routine primary care practice among those pharmacologically treated for elevated blood pressure, and free from cardiovascular comorbidities or diabetes mellitus.MethodWe assessed sex differences in the number of prescribed drugs,

title: A case of intra-abdominal textiloma mimicking a mesenteric tumor
creator: C Rhoul, M Mhand, M Inouss, Y Hamdaoui, T Bouhout, B Serji
description: IntroductionA textiloma or gossypiboma is a retained surgical material in the body after an operation. It may be asymptomatic or revealed by complications such as occlusion, perforation, and fistulization.Case reportWe report a case of intraabdominal textiloma mimicking a mesenteric tumor. The patient has a history of open cholecystectomy.

title: Neonatal carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I deficiency with severe hyperammonemic coma: the first report from Palestine
creator: Anas K Assi, Amro Odeh, Habeeb H Awwad, Hanin Kassem, Imad Dweikat
description: BackgroundCarbamoyl phosphate synthetase I deficiency (CPS1D) is the most proximal and severe urea cycle disorder, often presenting in the neonatal period with rapidly progressive hyperammonemia. Early symptoms are often nonspecific, posing significant diagnostic challenges and contributing to delays in targeted management.

title: IFPHOR0093 Access to Primary Health Care in the Asia-Pacific Region: Determinants, Impacts, and Strategic Interventions for Improved Equity
creator: Sabi Kaphle, Rasanthika Gunawardhana
description: BackgroundPrimary health care (PHC) is central to achieving universal health coverage and serves as the first point of contact within health systems. In the Asia-Pacific region (APR), access to PHC is shaped by diverse contextual and structural determinants that influence health outcomes and equity. Understanding these determinants is essential for informing effective policy and system responses.

title: IFPHPOS0038 Beyond Single Risk Factors: Environmental Clustering and Social Gradients in Childhood Asthma Severity
creator: Fatemeh Hoda Fallah, Philip McHale
description: BackgroundChildhood asthma is influenced by interactions between social and environmental determinants, particularly housing-related exposures. Traditional approaches focusing on single risk factors may underestimate cumulative environmental disadvantage. This study explored environmental risk clustering and socioeconomic gradients in asthma severity.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 246 children with physician-diagnosed asthma in Tehran.

title: Phase II randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to assess the efficacy and safety of MLC1501 in patients with stroke: the MLC1501 study Assessing Efficacy in post-STrOke Subjects with mOtor deficits (MAESTOSO) study protocol
creator: Christopher P L H Chen, Romulo U Esagunde, Cyrus G Escabillas, John Harold Hiyadan, Joel M Advincula, Christian Oliver C Co, Maria Epifania V Collantes, Annabelle Y Lao, Yeow-Hoay Koh, Deidre Anne De Silva, Carol Huilian Tham, Johnny K Lokin, Narayanaswamy Venketasubramanian
description: BackgroundMLC1501, consisting of four herbs, that is, Radix Astragali, Radix Angelicae sinensis, Rhizoma Chuanxiong, Radix Polygalae, has the same pharmacological properties as its precursors MLC601 and MLC901 which contain extracts of nine herbs and showed neuroprotective, anti-inflammatory and neurorestorative properties in non-clinical models, as well as clinical benefits in improving functional and neurological recovery after brain injuries.

title: False iliac artery aneurysms on a psoas abscess revealing tuberculosis disease: About a case report and review of the literature
creator: Asma Jdar, Mehdi Lekehal, Ayoub Bounssir, Tarik Bakkali, Brahim Lekehal
description: SummaryIntroduction and importanceTuberculosis is re-emerging globally, including in Morocco. Common iliac artery aneurysms induced by tuberculosis are very rare and severe due to the risk of infection and hemorrhage, making treatment choice crucial. Only a few cases have been reported in the literature.

title: IFPHOR0203 Associations between Urban Green and Blue Spaces (UGBS)’ Quality and Public Health in Greater Manchester
creator: Jingru Yang, Christine Greenhalgh, Greg Williams, Arpana Verma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Urban Green and Blue Spaces (UGBS), as an important component of the natural environment, are increasingly recognised as a potential solution to health challenges associated with urban sprawl and global urbanisation. While the health benefits of UGBS are shaped by both quantity and quality, evidence on the specific quality attributes of UGBS and their relationship to public health outcomes remains limited.This study adopts a mixed-methods approach to develop a conceptual framework for defining and characterising UGBS quality, with a particular focus on

title: Antibiotic consumption and prescription patterns in a tertiary care hospital in Karachi, Pakistan: a cross-sectional study
creator: Nosheen Nasir, Beenish Khalid Mehmood, Safia Awan, Alyna Khan, Saadia Sattar, Salma Tajuddin, Sonia Qureshi
description: BackgroundPakistan ranks third among low-middle-income countries (LMICs) in human antibiotic consumption. Moreover, it has alarmingly high antimicrobial resistance rates. Surveillance of antibiotic consumption rates can guide towards more responsible use. Our study aims to describe the antibiotic consumption and prescribing patterns in a tertiary care center in Karachi, Pakistan between 2016 and 2023.

title: Practical Aspects of Using Large Language Models to Screen Abstracts for Cardiovascular Drug Development: Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Jay G Ronquillo, Jamie Ye, Donal Gorman, Adina R Lemeshow, Stephen J Watt, Christian Lovis
description: Cardiovascular drug development requires synthesizing relevant literature about indications, mechanisms, biomarkers, and outcomes. This short study investigates the performance, cost, and prompt engineering trade-offs of 3 large language models accelerating the literature screening process for cardiovascular drug development applications. Introduction Cardiovascular drug development requires synthesizing information about indications, mechanisms, biomarkers, and outcomes [1,2].

title: IFPHOR0064 Waiting Well as Prevention: A Multi-Pathway Public Health Evaluation of Interventions Across Elective and Mental Health Waiting Lists
creator: Rochelle Velho, Katie Hibbitt, Ben Hollands, Jonathan Webster, Uma Walgama, Zafar Iqbal, Farah Kidy
description: BackgroundWaiting lists in England continue to rise, contributing to clinical deterioration, psychological distress and widening inequalities. Waiting periods are recognised as actionable intervals where targeted Wait List Interventions (WLIs) can mitigate harm rather than act as passive delays. This study synthesises evidence for WLIs across obesity, and adult & paediatric mental health pathways.

title: Chinese stroke association guidelines on reperfusion therapy for acute ischaemic stroke 2024
creator: Yunyun Xiong, Shuya Li, Chunjuan Wang, Dapeng Sun, Zixiao Li, HongQiu Gu, Aoming Jin, Qiang Dong, Liping Liu, Zhongrong Miao, Yongjun Wang, The Chinese Stroke Association Guidelines Writing Group on Reperfusion Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke
description: AbstractsBackgroundStroke remains a major global health challenge, with China experiencing a significant burden due to its high incidence and severe outcomes. Reperfusion therapies, such as intravenous thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy, have shown substantial benefits in improving early outcomes for ischaemic stroke.

title: IFPHOR0082 Indoor Air Quality Exposure in People with Cystic Fibrosis: Insights from the CF-Tracker Study
creator: Sharon Weinberg, Thomas J Bannan, Congbo Song, Eva Caamaño Gutiérrez, Robert W Lord, Rosmary E Maher, Andrew M Jones, Michael Tunney, Gordon McFiggans, Alexander Horsley
description: BackgroundIndoor and outdoor air pollution are major health risks. Indoor air quality (IAQ) contributes to over 90% of personal exposure. People with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) may be particularly vulnerable, as peaks in particulate matter (PM) and poor ventilation could trigger symptoms. However, indoor pollutant levels, their relationship with outdoor air, and their clinical relevance in CF remain poorly understood.

title: Barriers to and facilitators of women GPs’ careers: a systematic review
creator: Laura Jefferson, Elin Webster, Su Golder, Katie Barnett, Nicola Greenwood, Veronica Dale, Karen Bloor
description: BackgroundDespite women comprising 52% of full-time equivalent GPs in England, a significant gender pay gap persists (15% after adjustments). Further understanding of the barriers and facilitators impacting women GPs’ careers is needed.AimTo identify and synthesise research evidence exploring barriers to and facilitators of women GPs’ careers.Design & settingSystematic review of qualitative and quantitative studies.

title: Correction: Graphene quantum dots enhance the osteogenic differentiation of PDLSCs in the inflammatory microenvironment
creator: Wanshan Gao, Yan Liang, Dongyan Wu, Sicheng Deng, Rongmin Qiu
description: molecular characteristics of isolated PDLSCs. a, b microphotography of alive primary periodontal ligament cells (a) magnification 40×; (b) magnification 100×. c colony culture of PDLSCs and single-cell colony culture (inset panel). d microphotography of PDLSCs colony stained with Crystal Violet. e microphotography of representative data for Alizarin red-S staining of PDLSCs differentiates into osteoblasts.

title: 14th International Festival of Public Health
creator: Greg Williams, Gethin Hopkin, Elena Petelos, Tina Purnat, Laura Swain, Christine Greehalgh, Abin Thomas, Joanne Elliott, Jedidah Mould, Gary Clough, Arpana Verma
description: This year’s International Festival of Public Health marks our 14th year, and with the introduction of a dedicated supplement in the European Journal of Public Health, it seems appropriate to reflect on those years and the purpose of the Festival, including its place in the current world.

title: Association between video consultation use and general practitioner and practice characteristics: a cross-sectional survey in Denmark
creator: Thim Prætorius, Eskild Klausen Fredslund, Daniel Cæsar Torp, Annelli Sandbæk
description: BackgroundVideo consultations disrupt how general practice provides care and how patients receive it. A step towards understanding the use of video consultation is to study the association between user status and GP and practice characteristics.AimTo study the association between GP and general practice characteristics and video consultations user status (user, never user, and former user).

title: Examining use of restaurant nutrition information among adults living in England engaged in disordered eating or weight management efforts
creator: Alena F. Oxenham, Amanda Raffoul, Christine M. White, Lana Vanderlee, David Hammond, Michael Essman
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCalorie labels on menus are a popular policy initiative to help consumers to reduce their energy intake. Consumers trying to improve their diet may benefit from the labels if they help inform eating decisions.

title: Women’s Health
creator: Elizabeth Dalgarno, Joanne Elliott, Tina Purnat, Elena Petelos, Gethin Hopkin, Greg Williams, Jedidah Mould, Abin Thomas, Amy Wilcock, Laura Swain, Arpana Verma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Women and children’s health sits within a wider social justice framework where structural inequalities shape these outcomes across differing global contexts. Health is gendered, and we do not reflect this enough in research, service, product design and delivery. In the current polarised political environments, women’s health advocates are concerned that erosion of human rights, health services, and programmes is not just a line we need to defend from divestment.

title: Dynamical responses predict a distal site that modulates activity in an antibiotic resistance enzyme†
creator: Michael Beer, Ana Sofia F. Oliveira, Catherine L. Tooke, Philip Hinchliffe, Angie Tsz Yan Li, Balazs Balega, James Spencer, Adrian J. Mulholland
description: β-Lactamases, which hydrolyse β-lactam antibiotics, are key determinants of antibiotic resistance. Predicting the sites and effects of distal mutations in enzymes is challenging. For β-lactamases, the ability to make such predictions would contribute to understanding activity against, and development of, antibiotics and inhibitors to combat resistance.

title: Postcancer rehabilitation: multidisciplinary exercise – programme organisation and feasibility
creator: Chloé Drozd, Quentin Jacquinot, Sophie Paget-Bailly, Laura Mansi, Marie-Justine Paillard, Fernando Bazan, Loic Chaigneau, Erion Dobi, Julien Viot, Guillaume Meynard, Morgan Goujon, Lorraine Dalens, Victor Pereira, Edgar Robin, Jean Farret, Carole Gagnepain, Ophélie Simon, Christine Fagnoni-Legat, Fa
description: BackgroundAlthough the benefit of supportive care in the postcancer period is now well demonstrated, its implementation in the patient journey remains challenging. This article describes the development, since 2015 and in routine care, of supportive postcancer care comprising a multidisciplinary rehabilitation programme (MRP) based on exercise for patients with early breast cancer.

title: IFPHPOS0046 Operationalising Inclusive Research: Development and Pilot Testing of an Inclusive Research Maturity Matrix
creator: Eliza Varga, Joanne Elliott, Anna Coleman, Arpana Verma
description: BackgroundInequities in health outcomes are closely linked to unequal participation and representation in health research. Despite growing policy commitments, including the UK National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) inclusion strategy and “10 Steps to Inclusive Research,” there remains a lack of practical tools to operationalise inclusive principles across the research lifecycle.

title: Carriers of the m.3243A>G variant should not be labelled with an acronym before they have been systematically screened for multisystem disease
creator: Josef Finsterer
description: s), and kidney failure (niece).1 Two other family members (third sister, nephew) tested positive for the m.3243A>G variant.1 The study is compelling but raises concerns that should be discussed. The first point is that neither heteroplasmy rates nor mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copy number have been determined.

title: IFPHOR0088 Methods for Evaluating Usability in Healthcare Technology Assessment: A Critical Literature Review
creator: Tarteel Mohammedahmed, Alexander Thompson
description: BackgroundHealth technology assessment (HTA) provides structured evidence on the effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness of healthcare interventions. Yet usability - the extent to which technologies can be used by specified users with effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction - remains underdeveloped in HTA despite being crucial for adoption, workflow fit, and patient outcomes.

title: Mapping risk: Spatial analysis of 2,4-D herbicide emissions and colorectal cancer
creator: Danny Baxter, Dan A. Dixon, Andrew J. Morris, Tongzhang Zheng, Yong Zhu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Colorectal cancer remains a major public health concern in Arkansas and across the United States, disproportionately affecting rural and vulnerable populations. Beyond established lifestyle and genetic factors, environmental exposures, particularly agricultural chemicals, are increasingly recognized as potential contributors. In this ecological study, we screened 133 county-level estimated air pollutants to identify candidates associated with colorectal cancer incidence rates, focusing on Arkansas due to its agricultural economy and widespread herbicide use.

title: IFPHPOS0055 Lung Cancer Online Communities as a Mirror of Unmet Healthcare Needs: A Content Analysis of Topics, Emotions, and Misinformation
creator: Fatemeh Homayounifar, Elahe Meftah, Seyed Reza Abdipour Mehrian, Mahdi Salarabedi, Amirreza Jokar, Sadra Valiee, Hossein Molavi Vardanjani, Ali Amanati
description: BackgroundCancer patients increasingly turn to online communities for information and peer support, particularly in settings like Iran where financial burden, medication shortages, and unequal access to specialist care are common. These spaces offer emotional support but also risk spreading misinformation.

title: MHC class II genes influence the gut microbiota of wild golden snub-nosed monkeys
creator: Ji-Bing Yan, Tian-Qi Shi, Jin-Bang Zhang, Fei Long, Paul A Garber, Bao-Guo Li, Pei Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundGut microbiota play a critical role in host health and nutrition and are regulated by both non-genetic factors such as season, diet, habitat, age, sex, and genetic variation. Although researchers studying mammalian feeding ecology have focused principally on non-genetic influences of gut microbiota composition, there is growing awareness of the important role that genes coding for the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) play in enabling the host immune system to distinguish between beneficial and pathogenic microbes.ResultsHere, we examined MHC genes DRB1, DRB2, DQA1

title: IFPHOR0031 Working with Community Settings in North Somerset to Promote Oral Health
creator: Catherine Wheatley
description: BackgroundReduced oral health has implications for a person’s overall health and mental wellbeing. In England it is the responsibility of local authorities to improve the oral health of their populations. North Somerset Council began workforce training four years ago with early years professionals and has expanded into other sectors since.

title: Exploring complement activation as a therapeutic target in lupus nephritis
creator: Beom Jin Lim
description: s and plays a role in tissue damage associated with lupus nephritis [2]. The complement activation pathway in lupus nephritis has been the subject of extensive investigation for several decades [3]. All three activation pathways—the classical, alternative, and lectin pathways—participate in the tissue injury of lupus nephritis [2].

title: The energy crisis differentially impacted Swiss and German citizens’ energy literacy and efficiency preferences but not their support for climate policies
creator: Nina L Frings, Jessica F Helm, Ulf J J Hahnel
description: The energy crisis reshaped energy politics, resulted in energy price surges, increased energy capacity, and large-scale energy-saving campaigns. While an energy demand reduction was observed in Europe, little is known about how the crisis impacted citizens’ climate-relevant judgment and decisions.

title: Evaluation of immunoglobulin A1/immunoglobulin A2 ratio and B cell lymphoma-6 in relation to apoptosis-associated speck-like protein in diabetic kidney disease patients
creator: Sara Youssry, Hossam Ghoneim, Yasser Ammar, Azza Magdy, Dalia Maharem
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundInflammation and alteration of the immune system play a key role in the pathogenesis of diabetes mellitus (DM). However, little is known about the underlying mechanisms involved in the inflammatory pathways of diabetic kidney disease (DKD).

title: IFPHOR0068 Epidemiology and Outcomes of Acute Kidney Injury at a Tertiary Hospital in Johannesburg, South Africa: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Abdul Rhaman Kafagi
description: BackgroundAcute Kidney Injury (AKI) carries significant morbidity and mortality globally, yet data from sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce. South Africa presents a clinically distinct context characterised by high HIV burden, resource constraints, and formal rationing of kidney replacement therapy (KRT).MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted at Helen Joseph Hospital, Johannesburg.

title: Development and Implementation of an Interprofessional Education Course in Geriatric Care for Dental and Nursing Students
creator: Marianna Mantzorou, Theodoula Adamakidou, Georgia Gerogianni, Alexandra Koreli, Kalliopi Konstantopoulou, Anastassia Kossioni
description: IntroductionThis study aimed to describe the development and implementation of an interprofessional education (IPE) course in caring for older people for dental and nursing students and to investigate its impact on their perceptions of IPE and interprofessional collaborative practice (IPCP).MethodsThe IPE course was delivered to a convenience sample of 87 eighth semester dental and nursing students in a nursing home.

title: How did coronavirus disease 2019 affect autonomic balance in young individuals? Analysis by heart rate variability
creator: İmran Ceren, Fadime Bozduman Habip
description: SUMMARYOBJECTIVE:The aim of this study was to demonstrate the effect of coronavirus disease 2019 on the cardiovascular autonomic system using heart rate variability in young individuals.METHODS:The study was designed retrospectively by scanning the 24-h Holter electrocardiography records of patients who applied to the Ankara Abdurrahman Yurtaslan Oncology Education and Research Hospital Cardiology outpatient clinic.

title: Electroforming in VO2 Switch: Phase Transformation and Electromigration Phenomena
creator: Vanessa Conti, Cyrille Masserey, Victor Boureau, Anna Varini, Igor Stolichnov, Adrian Mihai Ionescu
description: Transition metal oxides provide a versatile platform for memristive devices, with vanadium oxide compounds attracting particular attention due to their sharp and ultrafast insulator-to-metal transition. However, their practical implementation is often constrained by structural and electrical modifications induced by high electric fields, commonly referred to as electroforming.

title: IFPHPOS0201 Women in Healthcare: Musculoskeletal Discomfort in Nurses, Evidenced from Resource-Limited Settings
creator: Upasana Chowdhury, Tamal Das, Somnath Gangopadhyay
description: BackgroundFemale nurses form the backbone of healthcare systems in low- and middle-income settings, yet their occupational health, especially musculoskeletal wellbeing, remains under-recognised. The nurses experience a dual burden of occupational strain and gendered expectations, making musculoskeletal health a critical women’s health concern.

title: Collagen type I alpha 2 acts as a potential diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic targets for the prognosis in gastric cancer
creator: Jingjing Dai, Xudong Song, Abdusemer Reyimu, Zihao Gao, Chenggong Zhang, Fan Ding, Dezhu Dai, Liang Shi, Xiao Han, Wubi Zhou, Guoquan Tao
description: BackgroundGastric cancer (GC) is a common digestive tract cancer whose high heterogeneity and invasiveness lead to a low survival rate. Therefore, it is necessary to explore the potential molecular mechanism of GC.MethodsThree genes and one miRNA expression microarray dataset were downloaded from the GEO database.

title: Analysis of Independent Risk Factors and Construction of a Risk Prediction Model for Non-Suicidal Self-Injurious Behavior in Adolescents with Depression
creator: Ying He, Shengying Dai, Tian Tang, Ying Ou
description: Background:The aim is to investigate the independent risk factors of non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) in adolescents with depression and to construct a risk prediction model to evaluate its predictive efficacy.Methods:Clinical data were collected from 150 adolescents diagnosed with depression who were admitted to West China Hospital of Sichuan University between October 2022 and October 2024.

title: IFPHOR0053 Evaluating the Leeds Community Vaccine Champion Programme: Building Trust and Connecting with Communities to Tackle Vaccine Inequality
creator: Kris Southby, Jenny Woodward, Laura Fitzgerald, Andrina Dawson, Ronnie Miley, Karl Witty
description: BackgroundFalling vaccination uptake has led to increases in preventable diseases such as measles across the UK. Disadvantaged and underserved communities, where uptake is lowest, are disproportionately affected, exacerbating health inequalities and leaving many individuals at risk (Flatt et al., 2024; UKHSA, 2025).

title: Content validation of the Myelofibrosis Symptom Assessment Form version 4.0 (MFSAF v4.0) in Janus kinase inhibitor–experienced patients with myelofibrosis
creator: Katelyn Cutts, Anna Cardellino, Shiyuan Zhang, Kelesitse Phiri, Heather Gelhorn
description: Patients with myelofibrosis (MF) experience debilitating symptoms that negatively impact health-related quality of life and functioning. The Myelofibrosis Symptom Assessment Form version 4.0 (MFSAF v4.0) is a 7-item questionnaire assessing the burden of MF symptoms, including fatigue, night sweats, pruritus, abdominal discomfort, pain under the left ribs, early satiety, and bone pain.

title: IFPHPOS0057 The Relationship Between Income-Generating Activities of Women, Dietary Behaviours and Feeding Practices of Infants and Young Children in Urban Ghana
creator: Jedidah Mould, Emily Rousham, Katherine Gough, James Esson
description: BackgroundMalnutrition remains a major public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, including Ghana, particularly among children aged 6–23 months, a critical window for growth and development. Maternal income-generating activities (IGAs) may influence infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices through improved income but also reduced caregiving time.

title: Bilateral carotid web successfully treated with endarterectomy, a case report
creator: Mohammed A Sadig, Abdullah G Alsahwan, Omar Alothman, Alwaleed S Althobaiti, Fahad Ahmed Z Alshammari, Faris Alomran
description: IntroductionA carotid web is an uncommon vascular anomaly that has been identified as an important cause of ischemic stroke in young patients with no traditional atherosclerosis risk factors. This fibrous membrane present in the internal carotid artery tends to cause turbulent flow and thrombosis. We report a case of bilateral carotid web successfully treated by carotid endarterectomy.

title: Photodynamic therapy using talaporfin sodium for grade 2/3 meningiomas: a preliminary study of safety, feasibility, and clinical outcomes
creator: Shinjiro Fukami, Jiro Akimoto, Kenta Nagai, Nobuyuki Nakajima, Norio Ichimasu, Ken Matsushima, Sho Onodera, Yuki Saito, Michihiro Kohno
description: PurposeAtypical and anaplastic (grade 2/3) meningiomas are associated with high recurrence rates and lack effective systemic therapies other than radiotherapy. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) using talaporfin sodium (TPS) generates selective cytotoxicity extending beyond resection margins and may improve local tumor control.

title: Prevalence of pulp canal obliteration after traumatic dental injuries: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Mariana Gouvêa Latini ABREU, Thaís de Oliveira FERNANDES, Leonardo Santos ANTUNES, Lívia Azeredo Alves ANTUNES, Lucianne Cople Maia de FARIA
description: This systematic review aimed to answer the following question: What is the estimated prevalence of pulp canal obliteration in subtypes of traumatic dental injury (TDI) in deciduous and permanent teeth? The searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, LILACS, Grey Literature, and Google Scholar, and complemented by a manual search, until April 16th, 2023.

title: IFPHOR0085 Dying to Give Birth: Uncovering the Cost of Inequality in British Maternal Healthcare
creator: Elisha Goma Moukala
description: The United Kingdom’s healthcare system, though globally recognised for its quality, exhibits stark racial disparities in maternal health outcomes. Black women in the UK are over four times more likely to die during pregnancy or the postnatal period compared to their White counterparts.

title: Cauda equina syndrome due to lumbar disc herniation managed with unilateral biportal endoscopic discectomy: A case report and review of literature
creator: Prakrit Chhetri, Bishnu Babu Thapa, Amir Ratna Shakya, Bimal Rai
description: Introduction and importanceCauda equina syndrome is a rare spinal emergency due to compression of the cauda equina nerve roots which present with bladder and/or bowel dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, and sexual dysfunction with or without a neurological deficit in the lower limbs and requires urgent surgical decompression through open methods or new minimally invasive procedures like Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Discectomy.

title: Progress in the study of product methodology development and competitiveness assessment model of voluntary carbon offsets
creator: Jin Han, Shaofeng Zheng, Jing Yuan, Congguang Zhang
description: This study focuses on methodological advancements in voluntary carbon reduction market products and the optimization of competitiveness evaluation models. Through systematic literature review, it analyzes the development characteristics, application scenarios, and existing challenges of international mainstream standards (VCS, GS, CDM) and domestic CCER and carbon credit methodologies.

title: Effectiveness of the Bivalent mRNA COVID-19 Vaccine for Preventing Critical Infection From the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron Variant in the Republic of Korea
creator: Young-Sook Choi, Sukhyun Ryu, Ryu Kyung Kim, Achangwa Chiara, Soojin Baek, Hojin Nam, Eunkyung Park, Eun Kyoung Kim, Young June Choe, Donghyok Kwon, Won Suk Choi
description: BackgroundThis retrospective observational matched cohort study assessed the differences in critical infections caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) during the omicron-predominant period of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. We evaluated the vaccine effectiveness of bivalent mRNA vaccine compared to unvaccinated individuals.MethodsWe collected COVID-19 case data from the Korean COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness cohort.

title: Initial pain score during viscous lidocaine instillation and clinical characteristics as predictors of overall pain in fusion prostate biopsy
creator: Gabriela M. Diaz, Lindsey T. Webb, Soum D. Lokeshwar, Ankur U. Choksi, Michael S. Leapman, Preston C. Sprenkle
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Prostate biopsy, while essential, often causes discomfort that can affect patient experience and adherence to follow-up procedures.Objective:This study aimed to identify factors associated with pain during fusion prostate biopsy to optimize the experience of prostate cancer diagnosis and monitoring.

title: Oral Collagen Peptides and Skin Rejuvenation: A Systematic Review and an Updated Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
creator: Asia Batool, Muhammad Sharjeel Abbas, Ramzan Farooq, Makhzan Ali Akbar, Alisha Ahmed, Warisha Kanwal, Hamza Ali, Ashfaq Ahmad, Muhammad Junaid, Muhammad Suhaib Hanif, Evardo Barros de Deus Nunes Junior, Hasibullah Aminpoor
description: BackgroundCutaneous aging is characterized by progressive degradation of the extracellular matrix, manifesting as diminished hydration, loss of elasticity, and increased wrinkle depth. While oral hydrolyzed collagen peptides (HCPs) are increasingly utilized as systemic nutricosmetics, previous evidence syntheses have been limited by severe methodological heterogeneity and the inability to account for highly influential statistical outliers.

title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Readmission Among Patients with Cardiovascular Diseases in Africa: A Systematic Review
creator: Frederick Acheampong Nimo, Edward Odoom, Abigail Gyamfi-Samakome, Hilda Kessewah Koranteng, Matthew Duah, Mildred Awinpiini Asore, Mustapha Amoadu, Nancy Innocentia Ebu Enyan
description: BackgroundCardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, with a disproportionately high burden in Africa. Readmissions among patients present an additional challenge.
